title.zh: 卷一百九十四 志第一百四十七 兵八
title.raw: 卷一百九十四 志第一百四十七 兵八 Volume 194 Treatises 147: Military 8

sentences.zh: 兵八○揀選之制廩給之制

translations.literal: Military 8 ○ Regulations on Selection; Regulations on Ration Allowances
translations.idiomatic: Military Affairs, Part 8: Regulations on Troop Selection and Ration Provisions

sentences.zh: 揀選之制建隆初，令諸州召募軍士部送闕下，至則軍頭司覆驗等第，引對便坐，而分隸諸軍焉。

translations.literal: On the system of selection: At the beginning of the Jianlong era, the various prefectures were ordered to recruit soldiers and escort them to the capital; upon arrival the Bureau of Military Heads would re-examine their grades, present them for audience at the informal throne, and assign them to the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations on selection: In the early Jianlong period, prefectures were instructed to recruit troops and send them to court. On arrival the Bureau of Military Heads reassessed their grades, presented them at an informal audience, and assigned them to the appropriate commands.

sentences.zh: 其自廂軍而升禁兵，禁兵而升上軍，上軍而升班直者，皆臨軒親閱，非材勇絕倫不以應募，餘皆自下選補。

translations.literal: Those promoted from garrison troops to the Imperial Guard, from the Imperial Guard to the upper army, and from the upper army to palace guard duty were all personally inspected before the throne; none were accepted for recruitment unless their talent and courage were matchless; all others were filled by promotion from below.
translations.idiomatic: Promotions from garrison troops to the Imperial Guard, from the Guard to the upper army, and from the upper army to palace guard roster all required a personal inspection before the throne. Only men of exceptional ability were taken on by recruitment; every other vacancy was filled by promotion from the ranks below.

sentences.zh: 咸平五年，於環、慶等州廂軍馬步軍六千餘人內選材勇者四千五百人，付逐砦屯防，以代禁兵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianping, from among more than six thousand cavalry and infantry garrison troops in Huan, Qing, and other prefectures, four thousand five hundred men of ability and courage were selected and assigned to garrison defense at each fort, to replace the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In 1002, from the six thousand-odd mounted and foot garrison troops in Huan, Qing, and neighboring prefectures, 4,500 able men were chosen and posted to individual forts for local defense, relieving Imperial Guard units of that duty.

sentences.zh: 景德二年，宣示：「殿前、侍衛司諸禁軍中老疾者眾，蓋久從征戍，失於揀練，每抽替至京，雖量加閱視，亦止能去其尤者。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingde, an edict proclaimed: "Among all the Imperial Guard units of the Palace Front and Palace Guard Bureaus, the old and infirm are numerous, because after long service on campaign and garrison duty they have not been properly screened; whenever rotations are brought to the capital, even if some review is added, only the worst cases can be removed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1005 the throne announced: "The Palace Front and Palace Guard commands hold many aged and sick troops. Years on campaign and frontier service have left screening neglected; when rotating detachments reach the capital we review them, yet can weed out only the worst cases.

sentences.zh: 今多已抽還，宜乘此息兵，精加選揀，雖議者恐其動眾，亦當斷在必行。

translations.literal: Now that most have been rotated back, we should take advantage of this lull in warfare to conduct a rigorous selection; although some in council fear disturbing the troops, the decision must be made to proceed without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Most units have now returned. We should use this pause in fighting to conduct a thorough selection. Critics may fear unsettling the ranks, but the matter must be decided and carried through.

sentences.zh: 昔太祖亦嘗患此，遂盡行揀閱，當時人情深以為懼，其後果成精兵。」

translations.literal: Formerly Taizu also worried about this and therefore conducted a full inspection; at the time people were deeply fearful, but afterward they indeed became elite troops."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had faced the same problem and ordered a complete inspection. Troops were deeply alarmed at the time, yet the force that emerged was genuinely elite."

sentences.zh: 樞密使王繼英等曰：「今兵革休息，不乘此時遴選，實恐冗兵徒費廩食。」

translations.literal: The Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wang Jiying and others said: "Now that arms are at rest, if we do not seize this moment to select carefully, we truly fear that redundant troops will waste rations in vain."
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wang Jiying and others replied: "With fighting at an end, failure to select troops now will only leave a bloated army consuming rations to no purpose."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "So it is.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Agreed.

sentences.zh: 近者契丹請盟，夏人納款，恐軍旅之情謂國家便謀去兵惜費。」

translations.literal: Recently the Khitan have sought alliance and the Xia have submitted; I fear the army will think the state now intends to cut forces and be stingy with expense."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan have lately sought peace and the Xia have offered submission. I fear the troops will read this as a sign that the court means to cut the army and pinch every coin."

sentences.zh: 乃命先於下軍選擇勇力者次補上軍。

translations.literal: He then ordered that brave and strong men be selected first from the lower army to fill vacancies in the upper army in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore ordered that the bravest men in the lower commands be promoted in turn to fill the upper army.

sentences.zh: 其老疾者，俟秋冬慎擇將臣令揀去之。

translations.literal: As for the old and infirm, wait until autumn and winter, carefully choose generals and officials, and have them screened out.
translations.idiomatic: The aged and infirm were to wait until autumn or winter, when carefully chosen officers would screen them out.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，詔遣樞密都承旨韓崇訓等與殿前司、侍衛馬步軍司揀閱諸軍兵士，供備庫使、帶禦器械綦政敏等分往京東、西路揀閱。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, an edict dispatched the Chief Coordinator of the Bureau of Military Affairs Han Chongxun and others, together with the Palace Front Bureau and the Palace Guard Cavalry and Infantry Bureau, to inspect all army soldiers; the Commissioner of the Arsenal and Bearer of Imperial Arms Qi Zhengmin and others were sent separately to inspect in the Eastern and Western Capital circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1006 an edict sent Chief Coordinator of the Bureau of Military Affairs Han Chongxun and others, with the Palace Front and Palace Guard cavalry and infantry commands, to inspect troops throughout the armies. Arsenal Commissioner and Bearer of Imperial Arms Qi Zhengmin and others were dispatched to conduct inspections in the Eastern and Western Capital circuits.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔效順第一軍赴京揀閱，以補虎翼名闕。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, an edict ordered the first army of Xiaoshun to come to the capital for inspection, to fill vacancies in the Tiger Wing roster.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the first Xiaoshun command was ordered to the capital for inspection, to fill vacancies in the Tiger Wing regiments.

sentences.zh: 是軍皆河東人，帝念其累戍勞苦，故升獎焉。

translations.literal: This army was entirely from Hedong; the emperor, mindful of their accumulated garrison hardships, therefore promoted and rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: The unit was entirely from Hedong. Mindful of their long frontier service, the emperor promoted and rewarded them.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符二年四月，詔曰：「江南、廣東西路流配人等，皆以自抵憲章，久從配隸，念其遠地，每用軫懷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu, fourth month, an edict said: "Those exiled to the circuits of Jiangnan and the Eastern and Western Guangnan have all brought the law upon themselves and long served in banishment; mindful of their distant lands, We are always moved to compassion.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of 1009 an edict declared: "Exiles in Jiangnan and the Eastern and Western Guangnan circuits have brought punishment on themselves and served long in banishment. Their distant posting moves Us to compassion.

sentences.zh: 屬喬嶽之增封，洽溥天之大慶，不拘常例，特示寬恩。

translations.literal: Now that Mount Qiao has received added enfeoffment and universal celebration pervades the realm, We set aside ordinary precedent and specially show lenient grace.
translations.idiomatic: With Mount Qiao newly enfeoffed and celebration spreading across the realm, We set aside ordinary rules and grant special clemency.

sentences.zh: 江南路宜差內殿崇班段守倫就升州、洪州，廣南東、西路差殿直、閣門祗候彭麟就桂州，與本路轉運使同勾抽諸州雜犯配軍，揀選移配淮南州軍牢城及本城。

translations.literal: For the Jiangnan circuit, Inner Hall Attendant Duan Shoulun should be dispatched to Sheng and Hong prefectures; for the Eastern and Western Guangnan circuits, Palace Attendant and Gate Aide Peng Lin should be sent to Gui prefecture, to join with the circuit transport commissioner in auditing miscellaneous offenders assigned to military service in the various prefectures, selecting them and reassigning them to the secure-garrison and local-garrison troops of Huainan prefectures and armies.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Shoulun, Inner Hall Attendant, should go to Sheng and Hong prefectures in Jiangnan; Peng Lin, Palace Attendant and Gate Aide, should go to Gui prefecture in Guangnan. Each is to work with the circuit transport commissioner to review miscellaneous convicts assigned to military service, select suitable men, and transfer them to secure-garrison and local-garrison units in Huainan.

sentences.zh: 有少壯堪披帶者，即部送赴闕，當議近上軍分安排。

translations.literal: Those young and strong enough to bear armor should be escorted to court at once; arrangements should be discussed for assignment to the nearest upper-army units.
translations.idiomatic: Young men fit to wear armor are to be escorted to court, where they will be assigned to the nearest upper-army commands.

sentences.zh: 如不願量移及赴闕者，亦聽。

translations.literal: If they do not wish transfer or coming to court, that too is permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Those who decline transfer or travel to court may remain as they are.

sentences.zh: 若地理遠處，即與轉運使同乘傳就彼，依此揀選。」

translations.literal: If the place is geographically remote, then together with the transport commissioner take relay horses and go there to conduct selection according to this."
translations.idiomatic: Where distance makes travel impractical, the commissioner may ride relay horses to the site with the transport official and conduct selection there."

sentences.zh: 五年正月，帝諭知樞密院王欽若等：「在京軍校差充外處人員，軍數不足，有妨訓練，可詔示殿前、侍衛馬步軍司簡補。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, the emperor instructed Wang Qinruo, Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and others: "When military officers in the capital are detailed to serve as personnel in outside posts, army numbers fall short and training is hindered; issue an edict to the Palace Front and Palace Guard cavalry and infantry bureaus to select and fill vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1012 the emperor told Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wang Qinruo and others: "Detailing capital officers to outside posts leaves commands understrength and disrupts training. Order the Palace Front and Palace Guard commands to select replacements.

sentences.zh: 禁軍逐指揮兵士內，捧日上三軍要及三百人，龍衛上四軍各二百五十人，拱聖、驍騎、驍勝、寧朔、神騎、雲武騎各三百五十人，並於下次軍營升填，須及得本額等樣，及令軍頭司於諸處招揀到人內選填。

translations.literal: Within each command of the Imperial Guard: the three upper armies of Sun-Bearer require up to three hundred men; each of the four upper armies of Dragon Guard requires two hundred fifty; Gong Sheng, Xiaoqi, Xiaosheng, Ningshuo, Shenqi, and Yunwuqi each require three hundred fifty—all to be filled by promotion from the next lower army camps, meeting the standard grades of the roster, and the Bureau of Military Heads is also to select and fill from recruits gathered in various places.
translations.idiomatic: Among Imperial Guard commands: the three Sun-Bearer upper armies need up to 300 men each; each of the four Dragon Guard upper armies needs 250; Gong Sheng, Xiaoqi, Xiaosheng, Ningshuo, Shenqi, and Yunwuqi each need 350—all filled by promotion from the next lower tier to roster standards, with the Bureau of Military Heads also filling gaps from recruits gathered nationwide.

sentences.zh: 營在京者引見分配，在外處者準此，仍委逐司擘畫開坐以聞。

translations.literal: Those encamped in the capital are to be presented for audience and assigned; those in outside posts follow the same rule; each bureau is still entrusted to plan and report the roster in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Units in the capital are to be presented and assigned accordingly; outside commands follow the same rule. Each bureau is to draw up detailed rosters and report.

sentences.zh: 在京差出者，候替回揀選。」

translations.literal: Those detailed out from the capital are to await replacement and return before selection."
translations.idiomatic: Officers detailed from the capital await their replacements' return before undergoing selection."

sentences.zh: 九年十一月，詔河北、河東、陝西諸州軍揀料本城兵，五百人以上升為一指揮，於本處置營教閱武藝，升為禁軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the ninth year, an edict ordered the various prefectures and armies of Hebei, Hedong, and Shaanxi to select local-garrison troops; where there were five hundred or more, they were to be raised to one command, camps established locally to drill martial skills, and promoted to the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of 1016 prefectures and armies in Hebei, Hedong, and Shaanxi were ordered to review local-garrison troops. Groups of 500 or more were to form a command, drill locally, and be promoted to the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年二月，遣使分往諸州軍揀廂軍驍壯及等者升隸上軍。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Tianxi, envoys were dispatched separately to the various prefectures and armies to select stalwart and qualified garrison troops and promote them to the upper army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 1017 envoys were sent to prefectures and armies across the empire to select strong, qualified garrison troops for promotion to the upper army.

sentences.zh: 六月，召選天下廂兵遷隸禁軍者，凡五千餘人。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, garrison troops from across the realm were summoned and selected for transfer to the Imperial Guard, totaling more than five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month more than 5,000 garrison troops empire-wide were selected and transferred to the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 天聖間，嘗詔樞密院次禁軍選補法：

translations.literal: During the Tiansheng era, the Bureau of Military Affairs was once ordered to draft regulations for Imperial Guard selection and filling of vacancies:
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiansheng period (1023–1032) the Bureau of Military Affairs was instructed to codify rules for Imperial Guard selection and promotion:

sentences.zh: 凡入上四軍者，捧日、天武弓以九斗，龍衛、神衛弓以七斗，天武弩以二石七斗，神衛弩以二石三斗為中格。

translations.literal: For entry into the four upper armies: Sun-Bearer and Heavenly Martial bow at nine dou; Dragon Guard and Divine Guard bow at seven dou; Heavenly Martial crossbow at two shi seven dou; Divine Guard crossbow at two shi three dou as the passing standard.
translations.idiomatic: Entry into the four upper armies required: Sun-Bearer and Heavenly Martial archers to draw nine dou; Dragon and Divine Guard archers seven dou; Heavenly Martial crossbowmen to span 2.7 shi; Divine Guard crossbowmen 2.3 shi as the passing mark.

sentences.zh: 恩、冀員僚直、驍捷軍士選中四軍，則不復閱試。

translations.literal: Soldiers of En and Ji Staff Attendant and Xiao Jie commands selected for the four armies were not re-examined.
translations.idiomatic: Men from the En and Ji Staff Attendant and Xiao Jie commands already chosen for the four upper armies were exempt from re-examination.

sentences.zh: 自餘招揀中者，並引對。

translations.literal: All others selected through recruitment were presented for audience.
translations.idiomatic: All other recruits who passed selection were presented at court.

sentences.zh: 凡員僚直闕，則以選中上軍及龍衛等樣、弓射七斗合格者充，仍許如龍衛例選補班直。

translations.literal: Whenever Staff Attendant vacancies occurred, men selected from the upper army and meeting Dragon Guard standards, with bow draw of seven dou, filled them; they were still permitted to be selected for palace guard duty by the Dragon Guard precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Staff Attendant vacancies were filled from the upper army by men meeting Dragon Guard standards who could draw seven dou, and they remained eligible for palace guard roster by the same rules as Dragon Guard troops.

sentences.zh: 凡選禁軍，自奉錢三百已上、弓射一石五斗、弩蹠三石五斗、等樣及龍衛者，並親閱，以隸龍衛、神衛。

translations.literal: For selection into the Imperial Guard: those with stipend of three hundred cash and above, bow draw of one shi five dou, crossbow span of three shi five dou, meeting grade standards and Dragon Guard level—all were personally inspected and assigned to Dragon Guard or Divine Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Guard recruits with a stipend of 300 cash or more who could draw 1.5 shi with the bow, span 3.5 shi with the crossbow, and meet roster standards—including Dragon Guard level—were all personally inspected and assigned to Dragon or Divine Guard.

sentences.zh: 凡騎御馬直闕小底，則閱拱聖、驍騎少壯善射者充。

translations.literal: Whenever junior vacancies occurred in the Imperial Horse Guard, young and strong archers from Gong Sheng and Xiaoqi were examined to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: Junior vacancies in the Imperial Horse Guard were filled by reviewing young, skilled archers from Gong Sheng and Xiaoqi.

sentences.zh: 凡弓手，內殿直以下選補殿前指揮使，射一石五斗；

translations.literal: For archers: from Inner Hall Attendant downward, selection to fill Palace Front command required draw of one shi five dou;
translations.idiomatic: Archers: promotion from Inner Hall Attendant and below to Palace Front command required a draw of 1.5 shi;

sentences.zh: 禦龍弓箭直選補禦龍直、禦龍骨朵子直，東西班帶甲殿侍選補長入祗候，禦龍諸直將虞候選補十將，射皆一石四斗；

translations.literal: Imperial Dragon bow and arrow guards selected to fill Imperial Dragon Guard and Imperial Dragon mace guards; Eastern and Western Hall armored palace attendants selected to fill senior palace attendants; Imperial Dragon guard squad leaders selected to fill squad chiefs—all required draw of one shi four dou;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Dragon bow guards filled Imperial Dragon and mace-guard posts; Eastern and Western Hall armored attendants filled senior palace attendant posts; Imperial Dragon squad leaders filled squad-chief posts—all required 1.4 shi;

sentences.zh: 東西班、散直選補內殿直，捧日、員僚直、天武、龍衛、神衛親從選補諸班直，禦龍骨朵子直、弓箭直將虞候選補十將，禦龍直長行選補將虞候，射皆一石三斗；

translations.literal: Eastern and Western Hall and general attendants selected to fill Inner Hall Attendant; Sun-Bearer, Staff Attendant, Heavenly Martial, Dragon Guard, and Divine Guard personal followers selected to fill various palace guard rosters; Imperial Dragon mace and bow guard squad leaders selected to fill squad chiefs; Imperial Dragon Guard senior ranks selected to fill squad leaders—all required draw of one shi three dou;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern and Western Hall and general attendants advanced to Inner Hall Attendant; Sun-Bearer, Staff Attendant, Heavenly Martial, Dragon, and Divine Guard personal followers to palace guard roster; Imperial Dragon mace and bow squad leaders to squad chief; Imperial Dragon senior ranks to squad leader—all required 1.3 shi;

sentences.zh: 員僚、龍禦、騎御馬直小底選補散直，射皆一石二斗。

translations.literal: Staff Attendant, Imperial Dragon, and Imperial Horse Guard junior ranks selected to fill general attendant—all required draw of one shi two dou.
translations.idiomatic: Staff Attendant, Imperial Dragon, and Imperial Horse Guard junior ranks advancing to general attendant all required 1.2 shi.

sentences.zh: 凡弩手，東西班帶甲殿侍選補長騎祗候，射四石；

translations.literal: For crossbowmen: Eastern and Western Hall armored palace attendants selected to fill senior cavalry attendants required span of four shi;
translations.idiomatic: Crossbowmen: Eastern and Western Hall armored attendants advancing to senior cavalry attendant required a span of 4 shi;

sentences.zh: 禦龍弩直將虞候選補十將，射三石八斗；

translations.literal: Imperial Dragon crossbow guard squad leaders selected to fill squad chiefs required span of three shi eight dou;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Dragon crossbow squad leaders advancing to squad chief required 3.8 shi;

sentences.zh: 長行選補將虞候，射三石五斗。

translations.literal: Senior ranks selected to fill squad leaders required span of three shi five dou.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ranks advancing to squad leader required 3.5 shi.

sentences.zh: 其捧日、天武、龍衛親從選補弩手班、禦龍弩直者，亦如之。

translations.literal: Sun-Bearer, Heavenly Martial, and Dragon Guard personal followers selected to fill crossbow squads and Imperial Dragon crossbow guards followed the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: Sun-Bearer, Heavenly Martial, and Dragon Guard personal followers selected for crossbow squads and Imperial Dragon crossbow guards followed the same standards.

sentences.zh: 其次別為一等，減二斗。

translations.literal: Next a separate grade was established, reduced by two dou.
translations.idiomatic: A second tier was then defined, two dou below the first.

sentences.zh: 自餘殿前指揮使、諸班直以歲久若上名出補外職者，所試弓弩鬥力皆遽減，弓自一石三斗至八斗，弩自三石二斗至五斗各有差。

translations.literal: For the rest—Palace Front commanders and various palace guard rosters who through long years or by senior listing took outside posts—the tested bow and crossbow strength was sharply reduced: bow from one shi three dou down to eight dou, crossbow from three shi two dou down to five dou, each with differences.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Front commanders and palace guard roster troops who through long service or seniority took outside posts faced sharply reduced tests: bow draw from 1.3 shi down to 0.8 shi, crossbow span from 3.2 shi down to 0.5 shi, tiered by rank.

sentences.zh: 凡班直經上親閱隸籍者，有司勿復按試。

translations.literal: All palace guard roster troops who had been personally inspected by the emperor and entered the rolls were not to be re-examined by the offices.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guard roster troops personally inspected by the emperor and entered on the rolls were exempt from further testing by the bureaus.

sentences.zh: 其升軍額者，或取少壯拳勇，或旌邊有勞。

translations.literal: Those promoted in army quota sometimes took the young and strong and brave in fist-fighting, sometimes honored frontier merit.
translations.idiomatic: Promotions in army quota favored either young men of exceptional strength or troops honored for frontier service.

sentences.zh: 至於河清遽補，牢城配軍亦間下詔選補，蓋使給役者有時而進，負罪者不終廢也。

translations.literal: As for the River Clearance command and sudden filling of vacancies, secure-garrison assigned troops also occasionally received edicts for selection and filling—so that those serving had times to advance, and those bearing guilt were not forever discarded.
translations.idiomatic: The River Clearance command and sudden vacancies were sometimes filled by edict from secure-garrison convict troops, so that men in service could advance in time and the guilty were not condemned forever.

sentences.zh: 其退老疾，則以歲首，或出軍回；

translations.literal: Retirement of the old and infirm took place at the year's beginning, or when troops returned from deployment;
translations.idiomatic: The old and infirm were retired at the New Year or when a unit returned from campaign;

sentences.zh: 轉員皆揀汰，上軍以三歲。

translations.literal: all rotations were screened and culled; the upper army every three years.
translations.idiomatic: every rotation was screened; the upper army every three years.

sentences.zh: 河北遇大閱亦如之。

translations.literal: In Hebei, when a grand review occurred, the same applied.
translations.idiomatic: In Hebei the same rule applied at grand reviews.

sentences.zh: 景祐元年，詔選教駿填拱聖諸軍，退其老疾為剩員，不任役者免為民。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyou, an edict ordered selection of trained chargers to fill Gong Sheng and other armies; the old and infirm were retired as surplus personnel; those unfit for service were released as civilians.
translations.idiomatic: In 1034 trained cavalry were selected to fill Gong Sheng and related commands. The aged and infirm became surplus rolls; men unfit for duty were discharged as civilians.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔選驍騎、雲騎、驍勝填拱聖，武騎、寧朔、神騎填驍騎。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict ordered selection of Xiaoqi, Yunqi, and Xiaosheng to fill Gong Sheng; Wuji, Ningshuo, and Shenqi to fill Xiaoqi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1036 Xiaoqi, Yunqi, and Xiaosheng were selected to fill Gong Sheng; Wuji, Ningshuo, and Shenqi to fill Xiaoqi.

sentences.zh: 康定元年，選禦輦官為禁軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangding, imperial carriage attendants were selected for the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In 1040 imperial carriage attendants were selected for the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 輦官二十六人遮輔臣喧訴，斬其首二人，餘黥隸嶺南，卒選如初。

translations.literal: Twenty-six carriage attendants blocked assisting ministers and clamored in protest; the two ringleaders were beheaded, the rest tattooed and assigned to Lingnan; in the end selection proceeded as before.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-six carriage attendants blocked a minister's path and protested loudly. Two ringleaders were beheaded; the rest were tattooed and sent to Lingnan. Selection then proceeded as originally ordered.

sentences.zh: 慶曆三年，詔韓琦、田況選京師奉錢五百已上禁軍武技精捷者，營取五人，樞密院籍記姓名，以備驅使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Qingli, an edict ordered Han Qi and Tian Kuang to select from the capital's Imperial Guard troops with stipend of five hundred cash and above those skilled and agile in martial arts, taking five men per camp; the Bureau of Military Affairs recorded their names for ready dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: In 1043 Han Qi and Tian Kuang were ordered to select from capital Imperial Guard units on 500-cash stipends or more the most skilled fighters, five per camp. The Bureau of Military Affairs registered their names for immediate dispatch.

sentences.zh: 況因言：「今天下兵逾百萬，視先朝幾三倍，自昔養兵之冗，未有若是。

translations.literal: Tian Kuang then said: "Today troops under Heaven exceed one million, nearly triple the previous dynasty; never in history has the redundancy of maintaining armies been like this.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Kuang added: "The army now exceeds one million men—nearly triple the previous reign. Never has the burden of maintaining troops been so great.

sentences.zh: 且諸路宣毅、廣勇等軍孱弱眾甚，大不堪戰，小不堪役。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Xuan Yi, Guang Yong, and similar armies of the various circuits are numerous and feeble—largely unfit for battle, barely fit for labor.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuan Yi, Guang Yong, and similar units across the circuits are numerous but feeble—too weak to fight, barely able to labor.

sentences.zh: 宜分遣官選不堪戰者降為廂軍，不堪役者釋之。」

translations.literal: Officials should be dispatched separately to select those unfit for battle and demote them to garrison troops; those unfit for labor should be released."
translations.idiomatic: Send officers to demote men unfit for combat to garrison status and discharge those unfit even for labor."

sentences.zh: 上然其言。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 皇祐元年，揀河北、河東、陝西、京東西禁廂諸軍，退其罷癃為半分，甚者給糧遣還鄉里。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangyou, Imperial Guard and garrison troops of Hebei, Hedong, Shaanxi, and the Eastern and Western Capital circuits were screened; the enfeebled were retired at half pay; the worst cases were given grain and sent back to their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: In 1049 Imperial Guard and garrison troops in Hebei, Hedong, Shaanxi, and the Eastern and Western Capital circuits were inspected. The enfeebled were retired at half pay; the worst were given grain and sent home.

sentences.zh: 係化外若以罪隸軍或嘗有戰功者，悉以剩員處之。

translations.literal: Those from beyond the frontier who had been assigned to the army for crimes, or who had once rendered battle merit, were all placed as surplus personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Men from beyond the frontier assigned to the army for crimes, or veterans with battle merit, were all placed on surplus rolls.

sentences.zh: 三年，韓琦奏：「河北就糧諸軍願就上軍者，許因大閱自言。

translations.literal: In the third year, Han Qi memorialized: "Among the grain-paid armies of Hebei who wish to join the upper army, permit them to speak for themselves at the grand review.
translations.idiomatic: In 1051 Han Qi memorialized: "Hebei grain-paid troops who wish to join the upper army should be allowed to petition at the grand review.

sentences.zh: 若等試中格，舊無罪惡，即部送闕，量材升補。」

translations.literal: If they pass the graded examination and have no prior offenses, escort them to court and promote according to ability."
translations.idiomatic: Those who pass the examination with no prior offenses are to be escorted to court and promoted according to ability."

sentences.zh: 乃詔四路都總管司：「自今春秋閱，委主管選長五尺六寸已上、弓一石五斗、弩三石五斗者，並家屬部送闕。

translations.literal: An edict then went to the four-circuit supreme command offices: "From now on at spring and autumn reviews, entrust the responsible officer to select men five chi six cun and above in height, bow one shi five dou, crossbow three shi five dou—and escort them with their families to court.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to the four frontier supreme commands followed: "At spring and autumn reviews hereafter, select men at least five chi six cun tall who draw 1.5 shi with the bow and span 3.5 shi with the crossbow, and escort them with their families to court.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐二年，詔神衛水軍等以五年，諸司庫務役兵以三年一揀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiayou, an edict ordered Divine Guard naval troops and others screened every five years; labor troops of the various bureau storehouses every three years.
translations.idiomatic: In 1057 Divine Guard naval units and similar commands were ordered inspected every five years; labor troops in government storehouses every three years.

sentences.zh: 五年，選京東西、陝西、河北、河東本城、牢城、河清、裝禦、馬遞鋪卒長五尺三寸勝帶甲者，補禁軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, from local-garrison, secure-garrison, River Clearance, armorers, and relay-post troops of the Eastern and Western Capital circuits, Shaanxi, Hebei, and Hedong, men five chi three cun and above able to bear armor were selected to fill the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In 1060 local-garrison, secure-garrison, River Clearance, armorer, and relay-post troops in the Eastern and Western Capital circuits, Shaanxi, Hebei, and Hedong who stood at least five chi three cun and could wear armor were selected for the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 其嘗犯盜亡坐黥者，配外州軍歸遠、壯勇。

translations.literal: Those who had committed theft, desertion, or tattooing offenses were assigned to outside prefecture armies as Guiyuan and Zhuangyong.
translations.idiomatic: Men convicted of theft, desertion, or branding were assigned to Guiyuan and Zhuangyong units in outer prefectures.

sentences.zh: 八年，右正言王陶奏：「天下廂軍以歲首揀，至於禁軍雖有駐紮還日揀法，或不舉。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Right Remonstrator Wang Tao memorialized: "Garrison troops empire-wide are screened at the year's beginning; as for the Imperial Guard, although there is a rule for screening on the day of return from garrison, it is sometimes not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In 1063 Right Remonstrator Wang Tao memorialized: "Garrison troops are inspected every New Year, but although Imperial Guard units have rules for inspection on return from garrison, the rule is often ignored.

sentences.zh: 臣竊惟調發禁軍本籍精銳，軍出之時尤當揀練。

translations.literal: Your servant reflects that dispatched Imperial Guard troops are by roster the elite; when the army goes out, screening is especially necessary.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Guard detachments are drawn from the elite roster; when troops deploy, screening is especially urgent.

sentences.zh: 請下有司，凡調發禁軍，委當職官汰年六十已上，將校年六十五已上衰老者，如此則兵精而用省矣。」

translations.literal: I request that the offices be ordered: whenever Imperial Guard troops are dispatched, entrust the responsible officer to cull those sixty years and above, and officers sixty-five and above who are aged—thus the troops will be elite and expenditure saved."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that whenever Imperial Guard units deploy, the responsible officer cull soldiers sixty and older and officers sixty-five and older who are infirm. The force will be sharper and costs lower."

sentences.zh: 下其章。

translations.literal: His memorial was forwarded down.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 殿前、馬步軍司奏曰：「舊制，遣戍陝西、河北、河東、廣南被邊諸軍悉揀汰，餘路則無令。

translations.literal: The Palace Front and Cavalry and Infantry Bureaus memorialized: "By old regulation, troops garrisoned in Shaanxi, Hebei, Hedong, and the border circuits of Guangnan were all screened and culled; other circuits had no order.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Front and cavalry and infantry commands replied: "Under old rules, units garrisoned in Shaanxi, Hebei, Hedong, and the Guangnan frontier were all inspected; other circuits had no such requirement.

sentences.zh: 請自今諸軍調發，悉從揀法。」

translations.literal: We request that from now on all troops dispatched follow the screening regulations."
translations.idiomatic: We ask that all future deployments follow the screening rules."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「凡選本城、牢城軍士以補龍猛等軍者，並案籍取嘗給奉錢五百及龍猛等者，以配龍猛；

translations.literal: Another edict said: "Whenever local-garrison and secure-garrison soldiers are selected to fill Dragon Fierce and similar armies, consult the registers and take those who once received stipend of five hundred cash and Dragon Fierce status, to assign to Dragon Fierce;
translations.idiomatic: A further edict ordered: "When selecting local-garrison and secure-garrison troops for Dragon Fierce and similar commands, consult the registers and assign men who once drew 500-cash stipends or served in Dragon Fierce to Dragon Fierce;

sentences.zh: 其不及等與嘗給奉錢四百以下，若百姓黥隸及龍騎等者，以配龍騎；

translations.literal: those below grade and who once received stipend of four hundred cash and below, or commoners tattooed and assigned, and Dragon Cavalry and the like, assign to Dragon Cavalry;
translations.idiomatic: men below grade who once drew 400 cash or less, commoners tattooed into service, and former Dragon Cavalry troops go to Dragon Cavalry;

sentences.zh: 其龍騎軍士戍還，即選填龍猛。

translations.literal: Dragon Cavalry soldiers returning from garrison are at once selected to fill Dragon Fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon Cavalry troops returning from garrison are immediately selected to fill Dragon Fierce vacancies.

sentences.zh: 自今本城、牢城悉三年一揀，著為令。」

translations.literal: From now on local-garrison and secure-garrison troops are all screened every three years—enacted as regulation."
translations.idiomatic: Local-garrison and secure-garrison troops are henceforth inspected every three years, enacted as permanent law."

sentences.zh: 治平元年，閱親從官武技，得百二十人以補諸班直。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiping, the martial skills of personal followers were reviewed; one hundred twenty men were obtained to fill various palace guard rosters.
translations.idiomatic: In 1064 the martial skills of imperial personal followers were reviewed; 120 men were chosen to fill palace guard roster vacancies.

sentences.zh: 乃詔：自今親從官，限年三十五以下者充。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered: from now on personal followers are limited to those thirty-five years and below.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: personal followers hereafter must be thirty-five years old or younger.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「如聞三路就糧兵，多老疾不勝鎧甲者，可勿拘時，揀年五十以上有子弟或異姓親屬等應樣者代之。

translations.literal: Another edict said: "As We hear, among the grain-paid troops of the three circuits many are old and infirm and cannot bear armor; do not wait for the scheduled time—screen those fifty and above who have sons, younger brothers, or collateral kin meeting the standards to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict noted: "Grain-paid troops on the three frontier circuits include many aged men who cannot wear armor. Do not wait for the regular inspection—select replacements fifty or younger with sons, brothers, or qualified collateral kin.

sentences.zh: 如無，聽召外人。」

translations.literal: If there are none, permit recruiting outsiders."
translations.idiomatic: Where no kin qualify, outsiders may be recruited."

sentences.zh: 是歲，詔京畿並諸路揀龍騎、壯勇、歸遠、本城、牢城、宣效六軍；

translations.literal: That year, an edict ordered screening in the capital region and all circuits of Dragon Cavalry, Zhuangyong, Guiyuan, local-garrison, secure-garrison, and Xuanxiao—the six armies;
translations.idiomatic: That year the capital region and all circuits were ordered to inspect Dragon Cavalry, Zhuangyong, Guiyuan, local-garrison, secure-garrison, and Xuanxiao—the six army types;

sentences.zh: 河清、車營、致遠、窯務、鑄錢監、屯田務隸籍三十年勝鎧甲者，部送京師填龍猛等軍；

translations.literal: those on the rolls of River Clearance, carriage camps, Zhiyuan, kiln works, coin-casting offices, and agricultural colonies for thirty years who could bear armor were escorted to the capital to fill Dragon Fierce and similar armies;
translations.idiomatic: men on the rolls of River Clearance, carriage camps, Zhiyuan, kiln works, mints, and agricultural colonies for thirty years who could wear armor were sent to the capital for Dragon Fierce and similar commands;

sentences.zh: 其自廣南揀中者，就填江西、荊湖歸遠闕額。

translations.literal: those selected from Guangnan filled Guiyuan vacancies in Jiangxi and Jinghu circuits on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: men selected in Guangnan filled Guiyuan vacancies locally in Jiangxi and the Jing-Hu region.

sentences.zh: 仍詔每三年以龍猛等軍闕數聞。

translations.literal: It was further ordered that every three years the vacancy numbers of Dragon Fierce and similar armies be reported.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years vacancy numbers for Dragon Fierce and similar commands were to be reported.

sentences.zh: 又詔諸路，有步射引弓兩石、廣弩四石五斗已上者，奏遣詣闕。

translations.literal: Another edict to the circuits: foot archers drawing two shi with the bow, or crossbowmen spanning four shi five dou and above, are to be memorialized and sent to court.
translations.idiomatic: Circuits were also ordered to send to court any foot archer drawing 2 shi or crossbowman spanning 4.5 shi or more.

sentences.zh: 二年，詔京東教閱補禁軍。

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict ordered the Eastern Capital circuit's drilled local garrison to fill the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In 1065 the Eastern Capital circuit's drilled local garrison was ordered to supply recruits for the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 先是，京東教閱本城，自初置即番隸本路巡檢，久不選補。

translations.literal: Previously, the Eastern Capital drilled local garrison, from its first establishment, rotated under the circuit patrol inspector and for long had no selection or filling of vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Capital drilled local garrison had from the outset rotated under the circuit patrol inspector and had long received no promotions.

sentences.zh: 上聞其軍多勇壯可用者，欲示激勸，故有是詔。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that this army had many brave and strong men fit for use and wished to show encouragement; therefore this edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard that the unit held many able fighters and wished to encourage them; hence the edict.

sentences.zh: 治平四年五月，揀選拱聖、神勇以下勇分，以補捧日、天武、龍、神衛闕數。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Zhiping, brave men were selected from Gong Sheng, Shenyong, and lower ranks to fill vacancies in Sun-Bearer, Heavenly Martial, Dragon, and Divine Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of 1067 brave men from Gong Sheng, Shenyong, and lower commands were selected to fill vacancies in Sun-Bearer, Heavenly Martial, Dragon, and Divine Guard.

sentences.zh: 元豐三年六月，權主管馬步軍司燕達言：「內外就糧退軍二十一指揮八千餘人，以禁軍小疾故揀退及武藝淺弱人配填，既不訓練，又免屯戍，安居冗食，耗蠹軍儲。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Yuanfeng, Acting Director of the Cavalry and Infantry Bureau Yan Da said: "Inside and outside, grain-paid retired troops in twenty-one commands, more than eight thousand men—filled with those screened out from the Imperial Guard for minor ailments and with men of shallow martial skill—receive neither training nor garrison duty, dwell at ease in redundant consumption, and drain military stores.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of 1080 Acting Director of the Cavalry and Infantry Bureau Yan Da reported: "Twenty-one commands of grain-paid retired troops inside and outside the capital—more than 8,000 men—are filled with men screened from the Imperial Guard for minor ailments and the martially inept. They receive no training, are exempt from garrison, live at ease on redundant rations, and drain military stores.

sentences.zh: 若自今更不增補，庶漸銷減，候有闕，依禁軍選募，教習武世，不數年間，退軍可盡變銳士。

translations.literal: If from now on no further filling is made, they may gradually be reduced; when vacancies occur, recruit by Imperial Guard selection, drill martial skills—in a few years the retired troops can all be transformed into sharp soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: If no further replacements are made, the rolls will shrink. When vacancies arise, recruit by Imperial Guard standards and drill martial skills. Within a few years these retired commands could become elite units.

sentences.zh: 內奉錢七百者減為五百，依五百奉錢軍等杖招揀。」

translations.literal: Those within on seven hundred cash stipend are reduced to five hundred; recruit and select by the standards of five-hundred-cash armies."
translations.idiomatic: Units on 700-cash stipends should be reduced to 500 and recruit by the standards of 500-cash commands."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 仍詔：「上四軍退軍改作五百奉錢軍額。」

translations.literal: An edict further ordered: "Retired troops of the four upper armies are reclassified as five-hundred-cash army quota."
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "Retired troops of the four upper armies are reclassified under the 500-cash quota."

sentences.zh: 八月，殿前、步軍司虎翼十指揮出戍歸營，閔其勞苦，詔並升補為神勇指揮。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, ten Tiger Wing commands of the Palace Front and Infantry Bureau returned from garrison to camp; mindful of their hardships, an edict promoted them all to Shenyong commands.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month ten Tiger Wing commands of the Palace Front and Infantry Bureau returned from garrison. Mindful of their hardship, an edict promoted them all to Shenyong commands.

sentences.zh: 廣西路經略司言：「雄略、澄海指揮闕額，請以諸路配送隸牢城卒所犯稍輕，及少壯任披帶者選補。」

translations.literal: The Guangxi circuit frontier commissioner said: "Xionglue and Chenghai commands have roster vacancies; we request to select from convicts escorted from various circuits assigned to secure garrison whose offenses were relatively light, and young men fit to bear armor, to fill them."
translations.idiomatic: The Guangxi frontier commissioner reported: "Xionglue and Chenghai commands have vacancies. We ask to fill them from lightly offending secure-garrison convicts escorted from other circuits and from young men fit to wear armor."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，提舉河北義勇保甲狄諮言：「舊制，諸指揮兵級內有老疾年五十五已上、有弟侄子孫及等杖者，令承替名糧，其間亦有不堪征役者，乞年四十已上許令承替。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year, fourth month, Di Zhe, Commissioner for Hebei Righteous Braves and Militia, said: "By old regulation, within each command rank, those old and infirm at fifty-five and above who had younger brothers, nephews, sons, or grandsons meeting the standards were ordered to inherit roster stipends; among them some were also unfit for campaign service. We request that those forty and above be permitted to inherit."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of 1081 Di Zhe, commissioner for Hebei righteous braves and militia, reported: "Under old rules, soldiers fifty-five or older who were infirm could pass their roster stipend to qualified younger kin. Some heirs were unfit for service. We ask that inheritance be allowed from age forty."

sentences.zh: 詔河北馬步諸軍依此。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hebei cavalry and infantry armies to follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei cavalry and infantry commands were ordered to follow suit.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔諸班直、上四軍，毋得簡常有罪改配人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, an edict ordered that various palace guard rosters and the four upper armies must not select men habitually guilty and reassigned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month palace guard rosters and the four upper armies were forbidden to recruit men with records of habitual offenses and reassignment.

sentences.zh: 元祐二年七月，詔諸路每歲於八月後解發試武藝人到闕，殿前司限次年正月，軍頭司限二月以前試驗推恩。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Yuanyou, an edict ordered that each year after the eighth month the circuits dispatch men testing martial arts to court; the Palace Front Bureau by the first month of the following year, the Bureau of Military Heads by the second month, to examine and grant favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of 1087 circuits were ordered each year after August to send martial-arts candidates to court. The Palace Front Bureau was to test them by the first month of the following year and the Bureau of Military Heads by the second, then grant rewards.

sentences.zh: 呈試武藝人同。

translations.literal: Those presenting martial-arts tests followed the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates presenting for martial-arts tests followed the same schedule.

sentences.zh: 三年閏十二月，樞密院言：「在京諸軍兵額多闕，而京東、西路就糧禁軍往往溢額。」

translations.literal: In the intercalary twelfth month of the third year, the Bureau of Military Affairs said: "Army quotas in the capital are largely vacant, while grain-paid Imperial Guard troops in the Eastern and Western Capital circuits often exceed quota."
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary twelfth month of 1088 the Bureau of Military Affairs reported: "Capital commands have many vacancies, while grain-paid Imperial Guard units in the Eastern and Western Capital circuits often exceed their quotas."

sentences.zh: 詔差官往逐路同長吏揀選發遣，以補其數。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched officers to each circuit to join with chief officials in selection and dispatch, to fill the numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Officers were sent to each circuit to work with local officials in selecting and dispatching troops to fill capital vacancies.

sentences.zh: 至若省並之法，凡軍各有營，營各有額。

translations.literal: As for the method of economizing through consolidation: every army had camps, every camp had quota.
translations.idiomatic: As for consolidation to save resources: every army had camps, and every camp had a fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 皇祐間，馬軍以四百、步軍以五百人為一營。

translations.literal: During Huangyou, cavalry took four hundred and infantry five hundred men per camp.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangyou period (1049–1054) a cavalry camp held 400 men and an infantry camp 500.

sentences.zh: 承平既久，額存而兵闕，馬一營或止數十騎，兵一營或不滿一二百。

translations.literal: After long peace, quotas remained but troops were vacant; one cavalry camp might have only several dozen riders, one infantry camp might not reach one or two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: After long peace the quotas remained on paper while ranks emptied: a cavalry camp might hold only a few dozen riders, an infantry camp fewer than two hundred.

sentences.zh: 而將校猥多，賜予廩給十倍士卒，遞遷如額不少損。

translations.literal: Yet officers were excessively numerous; grants and rations were ten times those of common soldiers; promotions by quota were not reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Officers multiplied, drawing grants and rations ten times a common soldier's pay, while promotions by quota went undiminished.

sentences.zh: 帝患之，熙寧二年，始議並廢。

translations.literal: The emperor was troubled by this; in the second year of Xining, consolidation and abolition were first discussed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was alarmed. In 1069 consolidation and abolition were first proposed.

sentences.zh: 陝西馬步軍營三百二十七，並為二百七十，馬軍額以三百人，步軍以四百人。

translations.literal: Shaanxi cavalry and infantry camps, three hundred twenty-seven, were consolidated to two hundred seventy; cavalry quota set at three hundred men, infantry at four hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi's 327 cavalry and infantry camps were merged into 270, with cavalry quotas set at 300 men and infantry at 400.

sentences.zh: 其後凡撥並者，馬步軍營五百四十五並為三百五十五，而京師、府界、諸路及廂軍皆會總畸零，各足其常額。

translations.literal: Thereafter wherever consolidation was applied, five hundred forty-five cavalry and infantry camps became three hundred fifty-five; the capital, metropolitan districts, circuits, and garrison troops all gathered scattered remnants, each filling its regular quota.
translations.idiomatic: Later consolidations reduced 545 cavalry and infantry camps to 355. The capital, metropolitan districts, circuits, and garrison forces all absorbed scattered remnants to restore regular quotas.

sentences.zh: 凡並營，先為繕新其居室，給遷徙費。

translations.literal: Whenever camps were consolidated, their quarters were first repaired and relocation expenses provided.
translations.idiomatic: Before any consolidation, quarters were repaired and relocation expenses paid.

sentences.zh: 軍校員溢，則以補他軍闕，或隨所並兵入各指揮，依職次高下同領。

translations.literal: Excess military officers were used to fill vacancies in other armies, or entered the various commands with the consolidated troops, leading according to rank high and low.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus officers filled vacancies elsewhere or joined consolidated commands by rank.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂輔臣曰：「天下財用，朝廷稍加意，則所省不可勝計。

translations.literal: The emperor once told assisting ministers: "The empire's finances—if the court pays slight attention, the savings cannot be fully calculated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told his ministers: "If the court pays even modest attention to state finances, the savings are beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 乃者銷並軍營，計減軍校、十將以下三千餘人，除二節賜予及傔從廩給外，計一歲所省，為錢四十五萬緡，米四十萬石，紬絹二十萬匹，布三萬端，馬槁二百萬。

translations.literal: Recently consolidating camps, it was calculated that more than three thousand military officers and squad chiefs and below were reduced; apart from biennial grants and attendant rations, the annual savings amounted to four hundred fifty thousand strings of cash, four hundred thousand shi of grain, two hundred thousand bolts of silk, thirty thousand bolts of cloth, and two million bundles of fodder.
translations.idiomatic: The recent camp consolidation cut more than 3,000 officers and squad chiefs and below. Apart from biennial grants and attendants' rations, annual savings came to 450,000 strings of cash, 400,000 shi of grain, 200,000 bolts of silk, 30,000 bolts of cloth, and 2 million bundles of fodder.

sentences.zh: 庶事若此，邦財其可勝用哉！」

translations.literal: If all matters were like this, how could state finances not suffice!"
translations.idiomatic: If every matter were handled this way, state finances would surely suffice!"

sentences.zh: 初議並營，大臣皆以兵驕已久，遽並之必召亂，不可。

translations.literal: When consolidation was first discussed, great ministers all said the troops had been arrogant for long; to consolidate abruptly would surely invite disorder—it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When consolidation was first proposed, senior ministers warned that troops had grown arrogant over years; abrupt merger would invite mutiny and must not be done.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，獨王安石讚決之。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen; only Wang Anshi praised and decided it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not hear them. Only Wang Anshi endorsed the plan and pressed it through.

sentences.zh: 時蘇軾言曰：「近者並軍蒐卒之令猝然輕發，甚於前日矣，雖陛下不恤人言，持之益堅，而勢窮事礙，終亦必變。

translations.literal: At the time Su Shi said: "Recently the order to consolidate armies and cull troops was rashly and lightly issued, worse than before; although Your Majesty does not heed people's words and holds firmer, when circumstances are exhausted and matters obstructed, in the end change is inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi said at the time: "The recent order to consolidate camps and cull troops was issued rashly—worse than before. Even if Your Majesty ignores criticism and holds firm, when circumstances reach an impasse change will come in the end.

sentences.zh: 他日雖有良法美政，陛下能復自信乎？」

translations.literal: Another day, though there be good laws and fine policies, can Your Majesty again have confidence?"
translations.idiomatic: When good policies arise later, will Your Majesty be able to trust them again?"

sentences.zh: 樞密使文彥博曰：「近多更張，人情洶洶非一。」

translations.literal: Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Wen Yanbo said: "Recently there have been many changes; popular sentiment is turbulent in more than one way."
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Wen Yanbo said: "Reforms have multiplied lately, and public unrest has many sources."

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「事合更張，豈憚此輩紛紛邪！」

translations.literal: Anshi said: "Matters ought to be changed—why fear this crowd's clamor!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi replied: "Reform is necessary. Why fear this clamor?"

sentences.zh: 帝用安石言，卒並營之。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted Anshi's words and in the end consolidated the camps.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sided with Wang Anshi and carried out the consolidation.

sentences.zh: 自熙寧以至元豐，歲有並廢。

translations.literal: From Xining through Yuanfeng, every year there was consolidation and abolition.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xining through Yuanfeng periods, consolidations occurred every year.

sentences.zh: 元符二年，樞密院言：「已詔諸路並廢堡砦，減罷兵將，鄜延、秦鳳路已減並，餘路未見施行。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfu, the Bureau of Military Affairs said: "An edict has already ordered the circuits to consolidate and abolish forts and stockades and reduce troops and officers; Fuyan and Qinfeng circuits have already been reduced and consolidated; other circuits have not yet been seen to implement it."
translations.idiomatic: In 1099 the Bureau of Military Affairs reported: "Circuits have been ordered to merge forts and reduce garrisons. Fuyan and Qinfeng have done so; other circuits have not yet complied."

sentences.zh: 詔涇原、熙河蘭會、環慶、河東路速議以聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jingyuan, Xihe Lanzhou-Huizhou, Huanqing, and Hedong circuits to deliberate quickly and report.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan, Xihe, Lanzhou-Huizhou, Huanqing, and Hedong were ordered to report plans promptly.

sentences.zh: 三年，罷都護府，安撫使隸河、蘭州，以省饋運。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Protectorate was abolished, and the Pacification Commissioner was subordinated to Hezhou and Lanzhou in order to reduce supply transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, the Protectorate was abolished, and the Pacification Commissioner was placed under Hezhou and Lanzhou to reduce the burden of supply transport.

sentences.zh: 詔邊帥減額外戍兵。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the frontier commanders to reduce garrison troops beyond the quota.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the frontier commanders to reduce extra-quota garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 建中靖國元年，減放秦鳳路土兵。

translations.literal: In Jianzhong Jingguo 1, local troops of Qin-Feng Circuit were reduced and released.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong Jingguo 1, the local troops of Qin-Feng Circuit were reduced and discharged.

sentences.zh: 大觀三年，詔：「昨降處分，措置東南利害，深慮事力未辦，應費不貲。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daguan, an edict said: "The disposition recently issued to arrange the advantages and disadvantages of the southeast deeply feared that resources were insufficient and expenses would be beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: In 1109 an edict noted: "Recent orders to secure the southeast risked overtaxing resources and spending beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 其帥府、望郡添置禁軍，諸縣置弓手，並罷其壯城兵士，令帥府置一百人，餘望郡置五十人，舊多者自依舊。

translations.literal: The added Imperial Guard at command headquarters and major prefectures, archers placed in every county, and strong-city troops are all abolished; command headquarters are to have one hundred men, other major prefectures fifty; where old numbers were greater, follow the old.
translations.idiomatic: Added Imperial Guard at command seats and major prefectures, county archers, and strong-city troops are all cancelled. Command seats keep 100 men, other major prefectures 50; where old quotas were higher, the old numbers stand.

sentences.zh: 沿邊州軍除舊有外，罷增招壯城。

translations.literal: Along the border prefectures and armies, apart from what already existed, cease additional recruitment of strong-city troops.
translations.idiomatic: Border prefectures and armies are to stop recruiting additional strong-city troops beyond existing rolls.

sentences.zh: 帥府、望郡養馬並步人選充馬軍指揮，及支常平錢收糴封樁斛斗指揮，並罷。

translations.literal: Command headquarters and major prefectures raising horses and selecting infantry to fill cavalry commands, and orders to disburse Ever-Normal Granary funds to purchase and store grain—all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Orders to raise horses at command seats, fill cavalry commands with infantry, and use Ever-Normal Granary funds to buy and store grain are all cancelled.

sentences.zh: 已添置路分鈐轄、路分都監，許令任滿。

translations.literal: Newly added circuit controllers and circuit chief inspectors are permitted to serve out their terms.
translations.idiomatic: Newly appointed circuit controllers and chief inspectors may serve out their terms.

sentences.zh: 江南東西、兩浙各共差走馬承受內臣一員、帥府添置機宜文字去處，並罷。」

translations.literal: Eastern and Western Jiangnan and the two Zhe circuits, each jointly dispatching one inner eunuch as relay commissioner, and places where command headquarters added policy secretaries—all abolished."
translations.idiomatic: The shared inner eunuch relay commissioners for Eastern and Western Jiangnan and the two Zhe circuits, and policy secretaries added at command seats, are all abolished."

sentences.zh: 四年，詔：「四輔州各減一將，其軍兵仰京畿轉運司將未足額並未有人，崇銳、崇威、崇捷、崇武內並廢四十四指揮已揀到人，隨等杖撥填四輔見闕禁軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict said: "Each of the four auxiliary prefectures reduces one general; its troops rely on the capital transport commissioner to take those below quota and without personnel; within Chongrui, Chongwei, Chongjie, and Chongwu, forty-four abolished commands already have selected men, to be allocated by grade standards to fill visible Imperial Guard vacancies in the four auxiliaries.
translations.idiomatic: In 1110 an edict ordered each of the four auxiliary prefectures to cut one general. The capital transport commissioner is to supply understrength units. Men already selected from forty-four abolished Chongrui, Chongwei, Chongjie, and Chongwu commands are to fill Imperial Guard vacancies in the four auxiliaries by qualification.

sentences.zh: 仍將逐輔係將、不係將軍兵，以住營遠近相度，重別分隸排定，及八將訓練駐紮去處，疾速開具以聞。

translations.literal: Further, take the troops under generals and not under generals in each auxiliary, measure by distance of encampments, reassign and arrange affiliations, and the eight generals' training and garrison locations—report quickly in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Troops under and outside generals in each auxiliary are to be reassigned by camp distance, with training and garrison sites for the eight generals reported promptly.

sentences.zh: 河北、河東崇銳、崇威，河東十八指揮，河北不隸將十三指揮並廢，見管兵令總管司撥填本路禁軍闕額。

translations.literal: Hebei and Hedong Chongrui and Chongwei, eighteen Hedong commands, thirteen Hebei commands not under generals—all abolished; present troops are ordered to the supreme command to allocate and fill this circuit's Imperial Guard vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei and Hedong Chongrui and Chongwei units, eighteen Hedong commands, and thirteen Hebei commands outside general jurisdiction are abolished. Surviving troops are to fill local Imperial Guard vacancies through the supreme command.

sentences.zh: 河北路撥不盡人發遣上京，分填在京禁軍闕額。

translations.literal: Hebei troops not fully allocated are sent to the capital and distributed to fill capital Imperial Guard vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei troops not placed locally are sent to the capital to fill capital Imperial Guard vacancies.

sentences.zh: 河東撥不盡人，並於本路禁軍額外收管。」

translations.literal: Hedong troops not fully allocated are all kept in this circuit beyond the Imperial Guard quota."
translations.idiomatic: Hedong troops not placed are retained within the circuit beyond regular Imperial Guard quota."

sentences.zh: 宣和五年，詔：「兩浙盜賊寧息，其越州置捕盜指揮，可均填江東、淮東三路州軍闕額。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuanhe, an edict said: "Bandits in the two Zhe circuits are pacified; the bandit-catching command established at Yue prefecture may evenly fill vacancies in the three circuits of Jiangdong and Huaidong prefectures and armies."
translations.idiomatic: In 1123 an edict noted: "With banditry quiet in the two Zhe circuits, the Yuezhou bandit-catching command may fill vacancies evenly across Jiangdong and Huaidong circuits."

sentences.zh: 至神宗之世，則又有簡汰退軍之令。

translations.literal: By the time of Emperor Shenzong, there were again orders to screen and cull retired troops.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shenzong came new orders to screen and retire redundant troops.

sentences.zh: 治平四年，詔揀拱聖、神勇以下軍補捧日、天武、龍衛、神衛兵闕。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiping, an edict ordered selection from Gong Sheng, Shenyong, and lower armies to fill vacancies in Sun-Bearer, Heavenly Martial, Dragon Guard, and Divine Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In 1067 troops from Gong Sheng, Shenyong, and lower commands were selected to fill Sun-Bearer, Heavenly Martial, Dragon Guard, and Divine Guard vacancies.

sentences.zh: 熙寧元年，詔諸路監司察州兵招簡不如法者按之，不任禁軍者降廂軍，不任廂軍者免為民。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xining, an edict ordered circuit overseers to investigate prefectural troops whose recruitment and selection did not follow law; those unfit for Imperial Guard were demoted to garrison troops, those unfit for garrison troops released as civilians.
translations.idiomatic: In 1068 circuit overseers were ordered to punish improper recruitment. Men unfit for the Imperial Guard were demoted to garrison status; men unfit even for garrison duty were discharged as civilians.

sentences.zh: 二年，從陳升之議，量減衛兵年四十以上稍不中程者請受。

translations.literal: In the second year, following Chen Shengzhi's proposal, stipends were reduced in measure for guards forty and above who slightly failed standards.
translations.idiomatic: In 1069, following Chen Shengzhi's proposal, stipends were reduced for capital guards over forty who barely missed standards.

sentences.zh: 呂公弼及龍圖閣直學士陳薦皆言退軍不便。

translations.literal: Lü Gongbi and Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall Chen Jian both said retiring troops was inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Gongbi and Dragon Diagram Hall academician Chen Jian both argued that retiring troops was impractical.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，司馬光亦曰：

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, Sima Guang also said:
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 1070 Sima Guang also said:

sentences.zh: 竊聞朝廷欲揀在京禁軍四十五以上微有呈切者，盡減請給，兼其妻子徙置淮南，以就糧食。

translations.literal: I have heard that the court intends to screen capital Imperial Guard troops forty-five and above who slightly show inadequacy, entirely reduce their stipends, and moreover relocate their wives and children to Huainan to draw grain rations.
translations.idiomatic: I hear the court plans to screen capital Imperial Guard troops forty-five and older who show slight inadequacy, cut their stipends entirely, and relocate their families to Huainan for grain-paid service.

sentences.zh: 若實有此議，竊謂非宜。

translations.literal: If this proposal truly exists, I privately deem it unsuitable.
translations.idiomatic: If this proposal is real, I believe it is unwise.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 在京禁軍及其家屬，率皆生長京師，親姻聯布，安居樂業，衣食縣官，為日固久。

translations.literal: Capital Imperial Guard troops and their families are mostly raised in the capital; kin and affines spread in networks; they dwell at ease in settled livelihoods; food and clothing come from the state—for days indeed long.
translations.idiomatic: Capital guards and their families were mostly born in the capital, with kin networks spread throughout the city. They have lived at ease on state rations for many years.

sentences.zh: 年四十五未為衰老，微有呈切，尚任征役，一旦別無罪負，減其請給，徙之淮南，是橫遭降配也。

translations.literal: Age forty-five is not yet old age; slight inadequacy still permits campaign service; suddenly, with no other guilt, reducing their stipends and relocating them to Huainan is to suffer arbitrary demotion and reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-five is not old. Slight inadequacy still leaves a man fit for duty. To cut his pay and exile his family to Huainan without any crime is arbitrary punishment.

sentences.zh: 且國家竭天下之財養長征兵士，本欲備禦邊陲。

translations.literal: Moreover, the state exhausts the empire's wealth to maintain long-service conscript troops, originally intending to guard the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The state spends the empire's wealth to maintain long-service troops precisely to guard the frontier.

sentences.zh: 今淮南非用武之地，而多屯禁軍，坐費衣食，是養無用之兵，置諸無用之地。

translations.literal: Now Huainan is no place for military use, yet many Imperial Guard troops are stationed there, sitting and consuming food and clothing—this is to maintain useless troops and place them in useless lands.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan is no theater of war, yet masses of guards would sit there consuming rations—useless troops in a useless place.

sentences.zh: 又邊陲常無事則已，異時或少有警急，主兵之臣必爭求益兵。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the frontier is usually without incident, that is one thing; another time, if there is slight alarm, commanders will surely compete to request more troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the frontier is quiet that is one matter; but at the slightest alarm frontier commanders will demand reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 京師之兵既少，必須使使者四出，大加召募，廣為揀選，將數倍多於今日所退之兵。

translations.literal: With capital troops already few, envoys must be sent in all directions, recruitment greatly expanded, selection broadly conducted—the numbers will be several times more than the troops retired today.
translations.idiomatic: With the capital already understrength, envoys will fan out to recruit widely. The new levies will be several times the men retired now.

sentences.zh: 是棄已教閱經戰之兵，而收市井畎畝之人，本欲減冗兵而冗更多，本欲省大費而費更廣，非計之得也。

translations.literal: This is to abandon troops already drilled and battle-tested and gather men from marketplaces and fields; originally intending to reduce redundant troops yet redundancy grows greater, originally intending to save great expense yet expense grows wider—not a winning plan.
translations.idiomatic: We would discard trained veterans for marketplace and field hands. The plan aims to cut redundancy yet will increase it; aims to save money yet will spend more. It is no winning strategy.

sentences.zh: 臣愚欲願朝廷且依舊法，每歲揀禁軍有不任征戰者減充小分，小分復不任執役者，放令自便在京居止，但勿使老病者尚占名籍，虛費衣糧。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly wishes the court for now to follow the old law: each year screen Imperial Guard troops unfit for campaign and reduce them to minor ranks; minor ranks again unfit for labor duty are released to dwell at will in the capital—but do not let the old and sick still occupy roster names and waste clothing and grain in vain.
translations.idiomatic: I urge the court to follow the old annual screening: demote guards unfit for combat to minor ranks; release minor ranks unfit for labor to remain in the capital—but remove the old and sick from the rolls so they no longer waste rations.

sentences.zh: 人情既安於所習，國家又得其力，冗兵既去，大費自省，此國家安危所係，不敢不言。

translations.literal: Once sentiment is settled in what they are accustomed to, the state also gains their strength; redundant troops are removed, great expense is self-reduced—this bears on the state's safety and peril; I dare not be silent.
translations.idiomatic: Men would remain where they are accustomed; the state would keep their strength; redundancy would fall and costs shrink. This bears on the state's safety—I dare not be silent.

sentences.zh: 右正言李常亦以為言。

translations.literal: Right Remonstrator Li Chang also spoke to the same effect.
translations.idiomatic: Right Remonstrator Li Chang made the same argument.

sentences.zh: 從之，是年，詔：「陝西就糧禁軍額十萬人，方用兵之初，其令陝西、河東亟募士補其闕。」

translations.literal: This was adopted; that year, an edict said: "Shaanxi grain-paid Imperial Guard quota is one hundred thousand men; at the beginning of using troops, order Shaanxi and Hedong quickly to recruit men to fill vacancies."
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed. That year an edict set Shaanxi grain-paid Imperial Guard quota at 100,000 men and ordered Shaanxi and Hedong to recruit urgently at the opening of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔：「比選諸路配軍為陝西強猛，其以為禁軍，給賜視壯勇為優，隸步軍司，役於逐路都監、總管司。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict said: "Recently selected assigned troops from various circuits for Shaanxi Strong Fierce—these are made Imperial Guard, grants superior to Zhuangyong, subordinate to the Infantry Bureau, serving under each circuit's chief inspector and supreme command."
translations.idiomatic: In 1071 an edict noted: "Assigned troops from the circuits recently selected for Shaanxi Strong Fierce are made Imperial Guard with grants above Zhuangyong levels, placed under the Infantry Bureau and circuit inspectors and supreme commands."

sentences.zh: 詔廣東、福建、江西選本路配軍壯勇者，合所募兵萬人，以備征戍。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Guangdong, Fujian, and Jiangxi to select strong men from this circuit's assigned troops, together with recruited troops totaling ten thousand men, to prepare for campaign and garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong, Fujian, and Jiangxi were ordered to select strong assigned troops and recruits totaling 10,000 men for campaign service.

sentences.zh: 三月，詔廣東路選雜犯配軍丁壯，每五百人為一指揮，屯廣州，號新澄海，如廣西之法。

translations.literal: In the third month, an edict ordered the Guangdong circuit to select sturdy men from miscellaneous offenders assigned to military service, five hundred per command, garrisoned at Guangzhou, titled New Chenghai, following Guangxi's method.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Guangdong was ordered to form commands of 500 sturdy convict soldiers each, garrisoned at Guangzhou as New Chenghai, following the Guangxi model.

sentences.zh: 七月，手詔：「揀諸路小分年四十五以下勝甲者，升以為大分，五十已上願為民者聽。」

translations.literal: In the seventh month, an imperial handwritten edict: "Screen minor ranks in the circuits forty-five and below who can bear armor and promote them to major ranks; those fifty and above who wish to become civilians are permitted."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month a handwritten edict ordered: "Promote minor-rank troops under forty-five who can wear armor to major rank. Men fifty and older who wish to leave service may do so."

sentences.zh: 舊制，兵至六十一始免，猶不即許。

translations.literal: By old regulation, troops were released only at sixty-one, and even then not immediately permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Under old rules discharge came only at sixty-one, and even then not immediately.

sentences.zh: 至是免為民者甚眾，冗兵由是大省。

translations.literal: At this time those released as civilians were very numerous; redundant troops were thereby greatly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Many were discharged as civilians, greatly reducing redundant troops.

sentences.zh: 十年，遣官偕畿內，京東西、陝西、荊湖長吏簡募軍士，以補禁軍之闕。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, officers were dispatched together with chief officials of the metropolitan districts, Eastern and Western Capital circuits, Shaanxi, and Jinghu to select and recruit soldiers to fill Imperial Guard vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1077 officers joined local officials in the capital districts, Eastern and Western Capital circuits, Shaanxi, and Jing-Hu to recruit soldiers for Imperial Guard vacancies.

sentences.zh: 六年，騎兵年五十以下，教武技不成而才可以肄習者，並以為步軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, cavalry fifty and below who failed to master martial skills in training but whose ability could still be cultivated were all made infantry.
translations.idiomatic: In 1073 cavalry under fifty who failed mounted training but could still be drilled were transferred to infantry.

sentences.zh: 元祐四年，詔：「今後歲揀禁軍節級，筋力未衰者，年六十五始減充剩員。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanyou, an edict said: "Hereafter in annual screening of Imperial Guard ranks, those whose strength is not yet declined are reduced to surplus personnel only at sixty-five."
translations.idiomatic: In 1089 an edict ordered: "In future annual screenings, Imperial Guard officers whose strength has not declined are reduced to surplus rolls only at sixty-five."

sentences.zh: 八年，涇原路經略司奏：「揀選諸將下剩員，年六十以下精力不衰，仍充軍，以補闕額。」

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Jingyuan circuit frontier commissioner memorialized: "Select surplus personnel under the various generals sixty and below whose vigor has not declined; still fill the army to supplement vacancies."
translations.idiomatic: In 1093 the Jingyuan frontier commissioner reported: "Select surplus personnel under generals who are sixty or younger and still vigorous to remain in service and fill vacancies."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 陝西諸路如之。

translations.literal: The various Shaanxi circuits did the same.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi circuits followed the same practice.

sentences.zh: 紹聖四年，樞密院言：「龍騎係雜犯軍額，闕數尚多。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaosheng, the Bureau of Military Affairs said: "Dragon Cavalry is a miscellaneous-offender army quota; vacancies are still numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In 1097 the Bureau of Military Affairs reported: "Dragon Cavalry is a convict-soldier quota with many vacancies still unfilled.

sentences.zh: 今欲將禁軍犯徒兵及經斷者，歲揀以填闕。」

translations.literal: Now we wish to take Imperial Guard convict soldiers and those already sentenced, screened annually to fill vacancies."
translations.idiomatic: We propose to fill them annually from Imperial Guard convicts and men already sentenced."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 元符元年又言：「就糧禁軍闕額，於廂軍內揀選年四十以下者填。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfu it was again said: "Grain-paid Imperial Guard vacancies—select from within garrison troops those forty and below to fill."
translations.idiomatic: In 1098 it was again proposed: "Fill grain-paid Imperial Guard vacancies from garrison troops forty and younger."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 宣和七年，詔京東西、淮南、兩浙帥司精選諸軍驍銳，發赴京畿輔郡兵馬製置使司。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xuanhe, an edict ordered the command offices of the Eastern and Western Capital circuits, Huainan, and the two Zhe to carefully select elite troops from all armies and dispatch them to the capital auxiliary prefectures army and horse disposition commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1125 command offices in the Eastern and Western Capital circuits, Huainan, and the two Zhe were ordered to select elite troops and send them to the capital auxiliary army disposition commissioner.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，詔：「軍兵久失教習，當汰冗濫，精加揀擇。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, an edict said: "Troops have long lost drill; redundant and excessive ranks should be culled and selection conducted with care."
translations.idiomatic: In 1126 an edict declared: "Troops have long gone undrilled. Redundant ranks must be culled and selection tightened."

sentences.zh: 然不能精也。

translations.literal: Yet in practice it could not be made rigorous.
translations.idiomatic: In practice the screening could not be made rigorous.

sentences.zh: 方兵盛時，年五十已上皆汰為民，及銷並之久，軍額廢闕，則六十已上復收為兵，時政得失因可見矣。

translations.literal: When troops were abundant, those fifty and above were all culled as civilians; after consolidation lasted long and army quotas were abandoned and vacant, then those sixty and above were again enrolled as soldiers—the gains and losses of policy of the time can thus be seen.
translations.idiomatic: When the army was large, men over fifty were discharged. After long consolidation left quotas empty, men over sixty were recruited again—the shifting fortunes of policy are plain to see.

sentences.zh: 中興以後，兵不素練。

translations.literal: After the restoration, troops were not habitually drilled.
translations.idiomatic: After the dynastic restoration, troops were no longer regularly drilled.

sentences.zh: 自軍校轉補之法行，而揀選益精。

translations.literal: Once the method of military officers transferring to fill vacancies was implemented, selection became increasingly rigorous.
translations.idiomatic: Once the system of officer promotion by transfer took effect, selection grew stricter.

sentences.zh: 大抵有疾患則選，有老弱則選，藝能不精則選，或由中軍揀補外軍，或揀外邊精銳以升禁衛。

translations.literal: Generally: if there was illness, then screen; if old or weak, then screen; if skill was not refined, then screen; or from central armies select to fill outside armies, or select frontier elite to promote to Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In general: the sick were screened out, the old and weak screened out, the unskilled screened out; central armies filled frontier vacancies, and frontier elites were promoted to the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 考《軍防令》，諸軍招簡等杖：天武第一軍五尺有八寸，捧日、天武第二軍、神衛五尺七寸三分，龍衛五尺有七寸，拱聖、神勇、勝捷、驍捷、龍猛、精朔五尺六寸五分，驍騎、雲騎、驍勝、宣武、殿前司虎翼、殿前司龍翼水軍五尺有六寸，武騎、寧朔、步軍司虎翼水軍、揀中龍衛、神騎、廣勇、龍騎、驍猛、雄勇、吐渾、擒戎、新立驍捷、驍武、廣銳、雲翼、有馬勁勇、步武、威捷、武衛、床子弩雄武、飛山雄武、神銳、振武、新招振武、新置振武、振華軍、雄武弩手、上威猛、廳子、無敵、上招收、冀州雄勝、澄海水軍弩手五尺五寸，廣捷、威勝、廣德、克勝、陝府雄勝、驍雄、雄威、神虎、保捷、清邊弩手、制勝、清澗、平海、雄武、龍德宮清衛、寧遠、安遠五尺四寸五分，克戎、萬捷、雲捷、橫塞、捉生、有馬雄略、效忠、宣毅、建安、威果、全捷、川效忠、揀中雄勇、懷順、忠勇、教閱忠節、神威、雄略、下威猛五尺四寸，亳州雄勝、飛騎、威遠、蕃落、懷恩、勇捷、上威武、下威武、忠節、靖安、川忠節、歸遠、壯勇、宣效五尺三寸五分、濟州雄勝、騎射、橋道、清塞、奉先、奉國、武寧、威勇、忠果、勁勇、下招收、壯武、雄節、靜江、武雄、廣節、澄海、懷遠、寧海、刀牌手、必勝五尺三寸，揀中廣效、武和、武肅、忠靖、三路廂軍五尺二寸。

translations.literal: Consulting the Military Defense Regulations, recruitment height standards for the various armies: Heavenly Martial First Army five chi eight cun; Sun-Bearer, Heavenly Martial Second Army, and Divine Guard five chi seven cun three fen; Dragon Guard five chi seven cun; Gong Sheng, Shenyong, Shengjie, Xiaojie, Longmeng, and Jingshuo five chi six cun five fen; Xiaoqi, Yunqi, Xiaosheng, Xuanwu, Palace Front Tiger Wing, and Palace Front Dragon Wing naval troops five chi six cun; Wuji, Ningshuo, Infantry Bureau Tiger Wing naval troops, selected Dragon Guard, Shenqi, Guangyong, Longqi, Xiaomeng, Xiongyong, and numerous frontier commands five chi five cun; Guangjie, Weisheng, Guangde, Kesheng, and related units five chi four cun five fen; Kerong, Wanjie, Yunjie, and related units five chi four cun; Bozhou Xionsheng, Feiqi, Weiyuan, and related units five chi three cun five fen; Jizhou Xionsheng, Qishe, Qiaodao, and related units five chi three cun; selected Guangxiao, Wuhe, Wusu, Zhongjing, and three-circuit garrison troops five chi two cun.
