translations.idiomatic: The Military Defense Regulations set recruitment heights by unit tier: five chi eight cun for Heavenly Martial First Army; five chi seven cun three fen for Sun-Bearer, Heavenly Martial Second Army, and Divine Guard; five chi seven cun for Dragon Guard; five chi six cun five fen for Gong Sheng, Shenyong, Shengjie, Xiaojie, Longmeng, and Jingshuo; five chi six cun for Xiaoqi, Yunqi, Xiaosheng, Xuanwu, and Palace Front Tiger and Dragon Wing naval units; five chi five cun for Wuji, Ningshuo, Infantry Bureau naval units, and a long list of frontier commands including Shenqi, Guangyong, Longqi, and crossbow units; five chi four cun five fen for Guangjie, Weisheng, Guangde, Kesheng, and related commands; five chi four cun for Kerong, Wanjie, Yunjie, and related units; five chi three cun five fen for Bozhou Xionsheng, Feiqi, Weiyuan, and related units; five chi three cun for Jizhou Xionsheng, Qishe, Qiaodao, and related units; and five chi two cun for selected Guangxiao, Wuhe, Wusu, Zhongjing, and three-circuit garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，詔：「江南、江東、兩浙諸州軍正兵、土兵、除鎮江、越州，委守臣兵官巡檢，六分中選一分，部轄人年四十五以下，長行年三十五以下，合用器甲，候旨選擇赴行在。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan, an edict said: "Regular troops and local militia of the various prefectures and armies of Jiangnan, Jiangdong, and the two Zhe circuits—except Zhenjiang and Yue prefectures—are entrusted to defending officials, military officers, and patrol inspectors to select one in six; escort personnel forty-five and below, senior ranks thirty-five and below, with proper armor and weapons, to await imperial selection and proceed to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: In 1129 an edict ordered defending officials and patrol inspectors in Jiangnan, Jiangdong, and the two Zhe circuits—except Zhenjiang and Yue—to select one man in six from regular and local militia troops. Escorts must be forty-five or younger, senior ranks thirty-five or younger, fully equipped, and held for dispatch to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 有軟弱不堪，年甲不應，或占庇不如數選發，其當職官有刑。」

translations.literal: If there are weak and unfit men, ages not matching requirements, or favoritism and protection causing shortfall in selection and dispatch, the responsible officials face punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Weak or overage men, or officials who shield favorites and fail to meet quotas, will be punished."

sentences.zh: 四年，詔：「神武義軍統製王燮下閱到第三等軍兵一千六百六十人，填廂禁軍，其不任披帶者，分填嚴州新禁軍。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict said: "Wang Xie, commander of the Divine Martial Righteous Army, reviewed and obtained third-grade troops numbering one thousand six hundred sixty men, to fill garrison Imperial Guard; those unfit to bear armor are distributed to fill Yan prefecture's new Imperial Guard."
translations.idiomatic: In 1130 an edict noted that Wang Xie, commander of the Divine Martial Righteous Army, reviewed 1,660 third-grade troops for garrison Imperial Guard service; men unfit for armor went to the new Yanzhou Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，上謂輔臣曰：「邵青、單德忠、李捧三盜，招安至臨安日久，卿等其極揀汰。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing, the emperor told assisting ministers: "The three bandits Shao Qing, Shan Dezhong, and Li Peng have been pacified and brought to Lin'an for long—ministers, conduct the most rigorous screening."
translations.idiomatic: In 1132 the emperor told his ministers: "Shao Qing, Shan Dezhong, and Li Peng were pacified long ago and have been in Lin'an. Conduct the strictest screening of their men."

sentences.zh: 呂頤浩、秦檜得旨與張俊同閱視，堪留者近七千人。

translations.literal: Lü Yihao and Qin Hui received the order and together with Zhang Jun conducted review; those fit to remain numbered nearly seven thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yihao and Qin Hui joined Zhang Jun in the review. Nearly 7,000 men were judged fit to remain.

sentences.zh: 詔命張俊選精銳，得兵五千人詣行在。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Zhang Jun to select elite troops; five thousand men were obtained and sent to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun was ordered to select elite troops; 5,000 were sent to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 二十年，樞密院言都統吳玠選中護衛西兵千人，詔隸殿司。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, the Bureau of Military Affairs said Supreme Commander Wu Jie selected one thousand western guard troops; an edict placed them under the Palace Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In 1150 the Bureau of Military Affairs reported that Supreme Commander Wu Jie had selected 1,000 western guard troops; an edict assigned them to the Palace Bureau.

sentences.zh: 又統製楊政選西兵三百二十五人，填步軍司。

translations.literal: Commander Yang Zheng also selected three hundred twenty-five western troops to fill the Infantry Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Yang Zheng also selected 325 western troops for the Infantry Bureau.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，詔：「禦龍直見闕數，可以殿、步二司選拍試填諸班。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, an edict said: "Imperial Dragon Guard visible vacancies may be filled by the Palace and Infantry bureaus through selection and trial shooting for various rosters."
translations.idiomatic: In 1154 an edict allowed the Palace Front and Infantry bureaus to fill Imperial Dragon Guard vacancies through trial shooting for palace guard roster posts.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年，詔王琪選三百人充馬軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiandao, an edict ordered Wang Qi to select three hundred men to serve as cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In 1166 Wang Qi was ordered to select 300 men for the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 慶元三年，殿司言：「正額效用萬一千五百九十二人，闕二百五十九人，於雄效內及效用帶甲拍試一石力弓、三石力弩合格人填闕額。」

translations.literal: In the third year of Qingyuan, the Palace Bureau said: "Regular quota utility troops eleven thousand five hundred ninety-two men, vacancies two hundred fifty-nine; from within Xiongxiao and utility troops in armor who pass trial shooting with one-strength bow and three-strength crossbow, fill vacancies."
translations.idiomatic: In 1197 the Palace Bureau reported: "Regular utility troops number 11,592 with 259 vacancies. Fill them from Xiongxiao and armored utility troops who pass trials with a one-strength bow and three-strength crossbow."

sentences.zh: 詔：「崇政殿祗候、親從填班直人數，特與免。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Chongzheng Hall attendants and personal followers filling palace guard roster numbers are specially exempt.
translations.idiomatic: An edict exempted Chongzheng Hall attendants and personal followers assigned to palace guard roster from the requirement.

sentences.zh: 其三衙舊司官兵及御馬直合揀班人，照闕額補。」

translations.literal: The three bureau old-office troops and Imperial Horse Guard due for roster screening are to fill according to vacancies."
translations.idiomatic: Troops of the three bureaus' old offices and the Imperial Horse Guard due for roster screening are to fill vacancies accordingly."

sentences.zh: 嘉定十一年，臣僚言「今軍政所先，莫如汰卒。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiading, a court official said: "In military administration today, nothing comes before culling troops."
translations.idiomatic: In 1218 a court official declared: "In military administration today, nothing takes priority over culling unfit troops."

sentences.zh: 謂「如千兵中有百人老弱，遇敵先奔，即千人皆廢矣。

translations.literal: They said: "If among a thousand troops a hundred are old and weak, and when they meet the enemy they flee first, then the whole thousand are rendered useless.
translations.idiomatic: They argued that if a hundred old and weak men lurked in a thousand-man unit and bolted at first contact, the entire thousand became worthless.

sentences.zh: 乞嚴敕中外將帥，務核其實。」

translations.literal: They begged that strict orders be issued to commanders inside and outside the court, and that they earnestly verify the facts."
translations.idiomatic: They asked that the throne issue stern orders to commanders throughout the empire to verify troop rolls in earnest."

sentences.zh: 其省並法自咸平始。

translations.literal: The method of consolidation and merger began in the Xianping era.
translations.idiomatic: The policy of consolidating and merging units dated from the Xianping period.

sentences.zh: 建炎以後，臣僚屢言，軍額有闕，則並隸一等軍分，足其舊額，以便教閱，而指揮、製領、將佐之屬亦或罷或省，悉從其請。

translations.literal: After the Jianyan era, court officials repeatedly memorialized that when army quotas had vacancies, commands were merged into a single army branch of equal rank to fill the original quota for ease of drill, and commanders, unit directors, and subordinate officers were sometimes abolished or reduced—all as they requested.
translations.idiomatic: After Jianyan, officials repeatedly urged that vacant army quotas be filled by merging commands into a single branch of the same tier, restoring full roster strength to simplify drill. Commanders, unit directors, and junior officers were sometimes cut or abolished, and each request was granted.

sentences.zh: 蓋當多事之秋，患兵之不足，望增補以壯軍容。

translations.literal: For in times of many crises, fearing insufficient troops, they hoped to increase and fill ranks to strengthen military presence.
translations.idiomatic: In troubled times, when troops seemed too few, the aim was to expand rosters and bolster the army's appearance of strength.

sentences.zh: 事既寧息，患其有餘，必並省以核軍實，意則在乎少蘇民力也。

translations.literal: When affairs had settled, fearing surplus, they invariably consolidated and reduced to verify actual troop strength—the intent being to give the people's resources some relief.
translations.idiomatic: Once crises passed and armies looked too large, consolidation followed to establish true troop counts—the underlying aim being to ease the burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 嘉熙初，臣僚言：「今日兵貧若此，思變而通之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jiading era, court officials said: "Today's troops are so impoverished—think of change to adapt.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiading period, officials declared: "The army is this poor today; we must find a way to change and adapt.

sentences.zh: 於卒伍中取強勇者，異其籍而厚其廩，且如百人之中揀十人，或二十，或三十，則是萬人中有三千兵矣。

translations.literal: From the ranks take the strong and brave, place them on a separate registry and increase their rations; for example, from a hundred pick ten, or twenty, or thirty—thus from ten thousand men there would be three thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Select the strongest and bravest from the ranks, register them separately, and increase their rations. Pick ten, twenty, or thirty from every hundred, and a nominal ten thousand would yield three thousand real fighters.

sentences.zh: 時試之弓弩，課之武藝，暇則馳馬擊球以為樂，秋冬使之校獵。

translations.literal: Periodically test them with bow and crossbow, assess their martial skills; in leisure let them ride horses and play cuju for pleasure; in autumn and winter organize hunts for them.
translations.idiomatic: Test them regularly with bow and crossbow and drill their martial skills. In off hours let them ride and play cuju for sport; in autumn and winter send them on organized hunts.

sentences.zh: 其有材力精強，則厚賞賚之。

translations.literal: Those of exceptional talent and strength receive generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Men of outstanding ability and strength were to receive generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 又於其中拔其尤者，數愈少而廩愈厚，待之如子弟，倚之如腹心，緩急可用。

translations.literal: Again from among them select the finest—the fewer in number, the richer the rations; treat them like sons and nephews, rely on them like trusted inner retainers—usable in urgency or emergency.
translations.idiomatic: From this elite pool, pick the very best: fewer in number but richer in rations, treated like family and trusted like one's inner circle—men who could be counted on when crisis struck.

sentences.zh: 蘇轍有言：『天子必有所私之將，將軍必有所私之士。』

translations.literal: Su Che once said: "The Son of Heaven must have favored generals; a general must have favored soldiers."
translations.idiomatic: Su Che had written: "The emperor must have generals he trusts personally, and every general must have soldiers he trusts personally."

sentences.zh: 又必申命主帥、製領，鼓動而精擇之，假之統御之權，嚴其階級之法。

translations.literal: Also orders must be conveyed to commanders and unit directors, they must be inspired and carefully selected, granted authority of command, and rank regulations strictly enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Orders must reach commanders and unit directors, who should be roused to careful selection, granted real command authority, and held to strict rank discipline.

sentences.zh: 將樂與士親，士樂為將用，則可以運動如意，不必別移一軍，別招新軍矣。」

translations.literal: When generals delight in closeness with soldiers and soldiers delight in serving their generals, then troops can be deployed at will—there is no need to transfer a separate army or recruit a new army."
translations.idiomatic: When generals and soldiers take pleasure in serving one another, forces can be moved as needed without transferring whole armies or raising new ones."

sentences.zh: 咸淳間，招兵無虛日，科降等下錢以萬計。

translations.literal: During the Xianchun era, recruitment went on without a single idle day, and rewards for lowering recruitment standards ran to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianchun period recruitment never paused for a day, and bounty payments for lowering enlistment standards ran into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 奈何任非其人，白捕平民為兵，召募無法，揀選雲乎哉！

translations.literal: Yet how could the wrong men be appointed—forcibly seizing civilians as soldiers, recruitment without method, and selection—what of that!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the wrong men were put in charge: civilians were seized and pressed into service, recruitment had no rules, and selection was a mockery.

sentences.zh: 廩祿之制為農者出租稅以養兵，為兵者事征守以衛民，其勢然也。

translations.literal: The system of rations and stipends: farmers pay grain taxes to support soldiers; soldiers serve in campaigns and garrisons to protect the people—such is the natural order.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations on Ration Provisions: farmers paid grain taxes to support the army; soldiers served on campaign and garrison duty to protect the people. Such was the natural arrangement.

sentences.zh: 唐以天下之兵分置藩鎮，天子府衛，中外校卒，不過十餘萬，而國用不見其有餘。

translations.literal: The Tang dispersed the empire's troops among frontier commands; the Son of Heaven's palace guards and central and external soldiers numbered no more than one hundred thousand and odd, yet state revenues never showed surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang, armies were scattered among frontier commands. Imperial guards and central troops totaled little more than 100,000, yet the treasury never showed a surplus.

sentences.zh: 宋懲五代之弊，收天下甲兵數十萬，悉萃京師，而國用不見其不足者，經制之有道，出納之有節也。

translations.literal: The Song rectified the ills of the Five Dynasties, gathered several hundred thousand armored troops from across the realm, and concentrated them all in the capital—yet state revenues never showed insufficiency, because systematic management was sound and disbursement was controlled.
translations.idiomatic: The Song corrected the abuses of the Five Dynasties by concentrating several hundred thousand armored troops in the capital. The treasury never ran short because management was systematic and spending was disciplined.

sentences.zh: 國初，太倉所儲才支三、二歲。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty, the Grand Granary's stores sufficed for only two or three years.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding, the Grand Granary held barely two or three years' supply.

sentences.zh: 承平既久，歲漕江、淮粟六百萬石，而縑帛、貨貝、齒革百物之委不可勝用。

translations.literal: After long peace, six million shi of grain were transported yearly from the Yangtze and Huai regions, while silk, goods, cowrie shells, ivory, leather, and a hundred other commodities accumulated beyond use.
translations.idiomatic: After decades of peace, six million shi of grain were shipped annually from the Yangtze-Huai region, and silk, goods, cowries, ivory, leather, and countless other commodities piled up beyond need.

sentences.zh: 其後軍儲充溢，常有餘羨。

translations.literal: Thereafter military stores overflowed, and surplus was common.
translations.idiomatic: Military stores soon overflowed, and surplus became the norm.

sentences.zh: 內外乂安，非偶然也。

translations.literal: Internal and external peace and order—this was no accident.
translations.idiomatic: The peace within and without the realm was no accident.

sentences.zh: 凡上軍都校，自捧日、天武暨龍衛、神衛左右廂都指揮使遙領團練使者，月俸錢百千，粟五十斛；

translations.literal: For all upper-army chief officers—from Sun-Bearer and Heavenly Martial through Dragon Guard and Divine Guard left and right wing commanders-in-chief who remotely held regiment-training commissioner posts—monthly stipend was one hundred strings of cash and fifty shi of grain;
translations.idiomatic: Upper-army chief officers—from Sun-Bearer and Heavenly Martial through Dragon and Divine Guard wing commanders who held honorary regiment-training commissioner titles—received monthly stipends of one hundred strings of cash and fifty shi of grain;

sentences.zh: 諸班直都虞候、諸軍都指揮使遙領刺史者半之。

translations.literal: palace guard roster deputy commanders and army commanders-in-chief who remotely held prefect posts received half that amount.
translations.idiomatic: palace guard roster deputy commanders and army commanders with honorary prefect titles received half as much.

sentences.zh: 自餘諸班直將校，自三十千至二千，凡十二等；

translations.literal: The remaining palace guard roster officers ranged from thirty strings to two strings, twelve grades in all;
translations.idiomatic: Other palace guard roster officers were paid in twelve grades from thirty strings down to two;

sentences.zh: 諸軍將校，自三十千至三百，凡二十三等，上者有傔；

translations.literal: army officers ranged from thirty strings to three hundred cash, twenty-three grades in all, the upper ranks having attendants;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Guard officers were paid in twenty-three grades from thirty strings down to three hundred cash, with attendants for the senior ranks;

sentences.zh: 廂軍將校，自十五千至三百五十，凡十七等，有食鹽；

translations.literal: garrison army officers ranged from fifteen strings to three hundred fifty cash, seventeen grades in all, with salt allowances;
translations.idiomatic: garrison troop officers in seventeen grades from fifteen strings down to three hundred fifty cash, with salt rations;

sentences.zh: 諸班直自五千至七百，諸軍自一千至三百，凡五等；

translations.literal: palace guard roster rank-and-file ranged from five strings to seven hundred cash; army troops from one string to three hundred cash—five grades in all;
translations.idiomatic: palace guard roster soldiers in five grades from five strings down to seven hundred cash; Imperial Guard rank-and-file from one string down to three hundred cash;

sentences.zh: 廂兵閱教者，有月俸錢五百至三百，凡三等，下者給醬菜錢或食鹽而已。

translations.literal: garrison troops under drill received monthly stipends from five hundred to three hundred cash, three grades in all; the lowest received only sauce-and-vegetable money or salt.
translations.idiomatic: drilled garrison troops received monthly stipends in three grades from five hundred down to three hundred cash; the lowest tier got only sauce-and-vegetable money or salt.

sentences.zh: 自班直而下，將士月給糧，率稱是為差；

translations.literal: From palace guard roster rank downward, officers and soldiers received monthly grain roughly according to grade differences;
translations.idiomatic: Below the palace guard roster, officers and soldiers received monthly grain rations scaled to rank;

sentences.zh: 春冬賜衣有絹綿，或加紬布、緡錢。

translations.literal: spring and winter clothing gifts included silk and cotton, sometimes supplemented with hemp cloth and strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: spring and winter clothing allowances included silk and cotton, sometimes supplemented with hemp cloth and cash.

sentences.zh: 凡軍士邊外，率分口券，或折月糧，或從別給。

translations.literal: Generally for soldiers on the frontier, ration tickets were usually split, or monthly grain was converted, or separate disbursements were made.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier soldiers generally received split ration tickets, converted monthly grain allowances, or separate disbursements.

sentences.zh: 其支軍食，糧料院先進樣，三司定倉敖界分，而以年月次之。

translations.literal: For the disbursement of military provisions, the Grain and Forage Bureau first submitted a sample; the State Fiscal Commission set granary boundaries, and distribution followed chronological order.
translations.idiomatic: Military grain was issued after the Grain and Forage Bureau submitted quality samples, the State Fiscal Commission fixed granary jurisdictions, and disbursements were scheduled by date.

sentences.zh: 國初，諸倉分給諸營，營在國城西，給糧於城東，南北亦然。

translations.literal: At the dynasty's founding, the various granaries distributed to the various camps: camps west of the capital received grain from the east of the city; the same applied north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, granaries distributed to camps by deliberate cross-town routing: units west of the capital drew grain from eastern warehouses, and the same rule applied north and south.

sentences.zh: 相距有四十里者，蓋恐士卒習墮，使知負簷之勤。

translations.literal: Distances of up to forty li were involved, lest soldiers grow accustomed to idleness and fail to know the labor of carrying grain on shoulder poles.
translations.idiomatic: Distances could reach forty li, lest troops grow soft and forget the labor of hauling their own rations.

sentences.zh: 久之，有司乃取受輸年月界分，以軍次高下給之。

translations.literal: Over time, the responsible offices took delivery dates and boundary divisions and distributed according to army rank precedence.
translations.idiomatic: In time the responsible offices abandoned the cross-town rule and issued grain by delivery schedule and army rank.

sentences.zh: 凡三歲大祀，有賜賚，有優賜。

translations.literal: Every three years at the major sacrifices there were bestowals and special grants.
translations.idiomatic: Every three years at the major state sacrifices there were standard grants and special bonuses.

sentences.zh: 每歲寒食、端午、冬至，有特支，特支有大小差，亦有非時給者。

translations.literal: Each year at Cold Food Festival, Dragon Boat Festival, and Winter Solstice there were special disbursements; the special disbursements varied in size, and sometimes off-schedule grants were also made.
translations.idiomatic: Cold Food, Dragon Boat, and Winter Solstice each brought special disbursements of varying size; occasional off-schedule grants were also made.

sentences.zh: 邊戍季加給銀、鞵鞋，邠、寧、環、慶緣邊難於爨汲者，兩月一給薪水錢，苦寒或賜絮襦褲。

translations.literal: Frontier garrisons received quarterly additions of silver and shoe money; along the Bin, Ning, Huan, and Qing frontier where cooking and drawing water were difficult, firewood money was given every two months; in severe cold padded jackets and trousers were sometimes granted.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier garrisons received quarterly silver and shoe allowances. In Bin, Ning, Huan, and Qing, where fuel and water were scarce, firewood money was paid every two months; in bitter cold, padded jackets and trousers were issued.

sentences.zh: 役兵勞苦，季給錢。

translations.literal: Corvée soldiers, for their hardship, received quarterly money.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée troops received quarterly hardship pay.

sentences.zh: 戍嶺南者，增月奉。

translations.literal: Those garrisoning Lingnan received increased monthly stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Troops garrisoning Lingnan received increased monthly stipends.

sentences.zh: 自川、廣戍還者，別與裝錢。

translations.literal: Those returning from garrison duty in Sichuan and Guang received separate travel outfit money.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers returning from Sichuan and Guangdong garrison duty received separate travel outfit allowances.

sentences.zh: 川、廣遞鋪卒或給時服、錢、履。

translations.literal: Relay-post runners in Sichuan and Guang sometimes received seasonal clothing, money, or shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Relay-post couriers in Sichuan and Guang sometimes received seasonal clothing, cash, or shoes.

sentences.zh: 屯兵州軍，官賜錢宴犒將校，謂之旬設，舊止待屯泊禁軍，其後及於本城。

translations.literal: Where troops were stationed in prefectures and armies, officials granted money to feast and reward officers—called the "ten-day provision"; originally this applied only to encamped Imperial Guard, but later it extended to local garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Stationed troops received official banquet funds for their officers, called the "ten-day provision." Originally limited to encamped Imperial Guard units, the practice later spread to local garrisons.

sentences.zh: 天聖七年，法寺裁定諸軍衣裝，騎兵春冬衣各七事，步兵春衣七事、冬衣六事，敢質賣者重置之法。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tiansheng, the Judicial Office fixed army clothing: cavalry received seven items each for spring and winter; infantry seven items for spring and six for winter; severe penalties were set for anyone daring to pawn them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1029 the Judicial Office standardized army clothing: seven spring and winter items for cavalry, seven spring and six winter items for infantry, with severe penalties for pawning issued gear.

sentences.zh: 景祐元年，三司使程琳上疏，論：「兵在精不在眾。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyou, State Fiscal Commissioner Cheng Lin submitted a memorial arguing: "Troops lie in quality, not in numbers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1034 State Fiscal Commissioner Cheng Lin memorialized: "An army's strength lies in quality, not head count.

sentences.zh: 河北、陝西軍儲數匱，而召募不已，且住營一兵之費，可給屯駐三兵，昔養萬兵者今三萬兵矣。

translations.literal: Hebei and Shaanxi military stores were repeatedly depleted, yet recruitment continued without cease; moreover, the cost of one encamped soldier could supply three stationed soldiers—what once maintained ten thousand troops now maintained thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei and Shaanxi stores were chronically short, yet recruitment never stopped. One encamped soldier cost as much as three locally stationed men; an army that once numbered ten thousand now numbered thirty thousand on paper.

sentences.zh: 河北歲費芻糧千二十萬，其賦入支十之三；

translations.literal: Hebei spent ten million two hundred thousand on fodder and grain yearly, while its tax revenue covered only three-tenths;
translations.idiomatic: Hebei spent 10.2 million on fodder and grain annually, while local tax revenue covered only three-tenths;

sentences.zh: 陝西歲費千五百萬，其賦入支十之五。

translations.literal: Shaanxi spent fifteen million yearly, while its tax revenue covered five-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi spent 15 million, while local revenue covered only half.

sentences.zh: 自餘悉仰給京師。

translations.literal: All the rest depended entirely on supplies from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Everything else came from the capital.

sentences.zh: 自咸平逮今，凡二邊所增馬步軍指揮百六十。

translations.literal: From the Xianping era to the present, both frontiers had added one hundred sixty cavalry and infantry commands in all.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xianping, the two frontier regions had added 160 cavalry and infantry commands.

sentences.zh: 計騎兵一指揮所給，歲約費緡錢四萬三千，步兵所給，歲約費緡錢三萬二千，他給賜不預。

translations.literal: Calculating the disbursement for one cavalry command, the yearly cost was about forty-three thousand strings of cash; for infantry, about thirty-two thousand strings—other grants and gifts not included.
translations.idiomatic: Each cavalry command cost roughly 43,000 strings of cash per year; each infantry command about 32,000—excluding other grants and bonuses.

sentences.zh: 合新舊兵所費，不啻千萬緡。

translations.literal: Combined costs for old and new troops amounted to no less than ten million strings.
translations.idiomatic: Total costs for old and new units ran to no less than ten million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 天地生財有限，而用無紀極，此國用所以日屈也。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth produce wealth in limited measure, yet expenditure knows no bounds—this is why state revenues daily grow strained.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth produce finite wealth, but spending knows no limit—that is why the treasury grows tighter by the day.

sentences.zh: 今同、華沿河州軍，積粟至於紅腐而不知用；

translations.literal: Now in Tong and Hua prefectures and armies along the Yellow River, grain piled up until it rotted red, yet went unused;
translations.idiomatic: Along the Yellow River in Tong and Hua, grain piled up until it rotted, unused;

sentences.zh: 沿邊入中粟，價常踴貴而未嘗足。

translations.literal: along the frontier, grain submitted in exchange for certificates constantly fetched soaring prices yet was never sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: while on the frontier, grain purchased through the contribution system always cost dearly and never sufficed.

sentences.zh: 誠願罷河北、陝西募住營兵，勿復增置，遇闕即遷廂軍精銳者補之，仍漸徙營內郡，以便糧餉。

translations.literal: I sincerely wish to abolish encamped recruitment in Hebei and Shaanxi and make no further additions; when vacancies arise, transfer elite garrison troops to fill them, and gradually move camps to interior prefectures to ease grain supply.
translations.idiomatic: I urge ending encamped recruitment in Hebei and Shaanxi and adding no new units. Fill vacancies with elite garrison troops and gradually move camps inland to ease logistics.

sentences.zh: 無事時番戍於邊，緩急即調發便近。

translations.literal: In peacetime rotate garrison duty on the frontier; in urgency dispatch the nearest available troops.
translations.idiomatic: In peacetime rotate frontier garrison duty; in crisis dispatch the nearest available forces.

sentences.zh: 嚴戒封疆之臣，毋得侵軼生事以覬恩賞，違令者重寘之法。

translations.literal: Strictly warn frontier officials not to raid or provoke incidents in hopes of favor and reward; violators face severe punishment by law.
translations.idiomatic: Strictly warn frontier officials against raiding or provoking incidents to win rewards; violators should face heavy penalties.

sentences.zh: 如此，則疆場無事，而國用有餘矣。」

translations.literal: Thus the frontier would be peaceful and state revenues would have surplus."
translations.idiomatic: Then the frontier would stay quiet and the treasury would have surplus."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the proposal and adopted it.

sentences.zh: 康定元年，詔戰場士卒給奉終其身。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangding, an edict granted soldiers wounded on the battlefield stipends for life.
translations.idiomatic: In 1040 an edict granted soldiers disabled in battle lifetime stipends.

sentences.zh: 宰臣張士遜等言禁兵久戍邊。

translations.literal: Chancellor Zhang Shisun and others said the Imperial Guard had long garrisoned the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Zhang Shisun and others reported that Imperial Guard troops had long garrisoned the frontier.

sentences.zh: 其家在京師者，或不能自給。

translations.literal: Their families in the capital sometimes could not support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Families left behind in the capital sometimes could not support themselves.

sentences.zh: 帝召內侍即殿隅條軍校而下為數等，特出內藏庫緡錢十萬賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned a eunuch to the palace corner and listed military officers by rank into several grades, specially disbursing one hundred thousand strings of cash from the inner treasury to grant them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had a eunuch rank officers by grade at a palace corner and specially disbursed 100,000 strings of cash from the inner treasury as a grant.

sentences.zh: 慶曆五年，詔：「湖南路發卒征蠻，以給裝錢者，毋得更予帶甲錢。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qingli, an edict said: "For Hunan Circuit troops dispatched against the barbarians, those who have received travel outfit money shall not also receive armor money."
translations.idiomatic: In 1045 an edict ruled: "Hunan troops sent against the barbarians who receive travel outfit allowances shall not also receive armor money."

sentences.zh: 七年，帝因閱軍糧，諭倉官曰：「自今後當足數給之。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the emperor, while reviewing military grain, instructed the granary officials: "From now on full measures shall be issued."
translations.idiomatic: In 1047, while inspecting military grain, the emperor told granary officials: "Issue full rations from now on."

sentences.zh: 初，有司以糧漕自江、淮，積年而後支，惟上軍所給斗升僅足，中、下軍率十得八九而已。

translations.literal: Previously, because grain was transported from the Yangtze and Huai and accumulated for years before disbursement, only the upper army received full measures by the dou and sheng; middle and lower armies on average received only eight or nine parts in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, because Yangtze-Huai grain took years to reach frontier stores, only upper-army units received full measure; middle and lower units typically got only eight or nine parts in ten.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐八年，殿前諸班請糧，比進樣異，輒不受散去。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiayou, the various palace guard rosters of the Palace Front requested grain; when it differed from the submitted sample they refused it and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1063 Palace Front guard rosters refused grain that did not match the submitted quality sample and dispersed in protest.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞王疇以為言。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wang Chou reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wang Chou brought the incident to the throne's attention.

sentences.zh: 詔：「提點倉官自今往檢視，有不如樣，同坐之。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Granary supervisors shall hereafter inspect in person; if grain is not up to sample, they share punishment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered: "Granary supervisors must inspect deliveries in person hereafter; if grain fails the sample standard, they share the penalty.

sentences.zh: 軍士不時請及有喧嘩，悉從軍法。」

translations.literal: Soldiers who do not request rations on schedule and cause uproar—all shall be handled under military law."
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers who fail to collect rations on time or cause disturbances shall all be punished under military law."

sentences.zh: 皇祐二年，詔：「在外禁軍，凡郊賚折色，並給以實估之直。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangyou, an edict said: "For Imperial Guard units outside the capital, all suburban-sacrifice grants paid in converted goods shall be paid at actual appraised value."
translations.idiomatic: In 1050 an edict ruled: "Imperial Guard units posted outside the capital shall receive suburban-sacrifice grants in converted goods at full appraised value."

sentences.zh: 五年，詔：「廣南捕蠻諸軍歲滿歸營，人賜錢二千，月增奉錢二百。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict said: "Guangnan anti-barbarian armies, upon completing their term and returning to camp, shall each receive two thousand cash, with monthly stipend increased by two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In 1053 an edict granted Guangnan anti-barbarian units, on completing their term and returning to camp, two thousand cash each plus a two-hundred-cash increase in monthly stipend.

sentences.zh: 度嶺陣亡及瘴癘物故者子孫或弟侄，不以等樣收一人隸本營者，支衣廩之半。」

translations.literal: For those who died in battle crossing the mountains or perished from miasma, if a descendant or nephew was enrolled in the original camp without regard to standard qualifications, half clothing and rations were disbursed."
translations.idiomatic: If a descendant or nephew of a soldier killed crossing the mountains or dead of miasma was enrolled in the original camp regardless of standard qualifications, half the usual clothing and ration allowance was granted."

sentences.zh: 治平二年，詔：「涇原勇毅軍揀為三等，差給奉錢一千至五百為三等，勿復置營，以季集渭州按閱。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiping, an edict said: "The Jingyuan Brave Resolute Army shall be screened into three grades, with stipends differentially granted from one thousand to five hundred cash in three grades; permanent camps shall not be re-established; they shall assemble quarterly at Weizhou for inspection."
translations.idiomatic: In 1065 an edict screened the Jingyuan Brave Resolute Army into three grades with stipends from 1,000 down to 500 cash, abolished permanent camps, and ordered quarterly musters at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 熙寧三年，帝手詔：「倉使給軍糧，例有虧減，出軍之家，侵牟益甚，豈朕所以愛養將士意哉！

translations.literal: In the third year of Xining, the emperor's handwritten edict said: "Granary officials issuing military grain routinely shortchange the amounts; families of soldiers on campaign suffer even worse exploitation—is this my intent in caring for officers and soldiers!
translations.idiomatic: In 1070 the emperor wrote by hand: "Granary officials routinely shortchange military grain issues, and the families of deployed soldiers suffer worst of all—is this how I mean to care for my troops?

sentences.zh: 自今給糧毋損其數，三司具為令。」

translations.literal: From now on grain shall be issued without reducing the amount; the State Fiscal Commission shall fully codify this as regulation."
translations.idiomatic: Issue full rations from now on, and let the State Fiscal Commission codify the rule."

sentences.zh: 於是嚴河倉乞取減刻之事。

translations.literal: Thereupon strict penalties were imposed for Yellow River granary officials who begged for and deducted grain.
translations.idiomatic: Strict penalties followed for Yellow River granary officials who solicited bribes and shortchanged rations.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔付趙禼：「聞鄜延路諸軍數出，至鬻衣裝以自給，可密體量振恤之。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict was entrusted to Zhao Xu: "I hear that troops of the Yan-yan Route are frequently deployed, to the point of selling their equipment to support themselves—secretly assess the situation and provide relief."
translations.idiomatic: In 1071 an edict sent Zhao Xu to investigate: "Troops on the Yan-yan Route are deployed so often they sell their gear to survive—assess the situation discreetly and provide relief."

sentences.zh: 先是，王安石言：「今士卒極窘，至有衣紙而擐甲者，此最為大憂，而自來將帥不敢言振恤士卒，恐成姑息，以致兵驕。

translations.literal: Previously, Wang Anshi said: "Today's soldiers are extremely destitute—some wear paper under their armor; this is the greatest worry. Yet commanders have never dared speak of relief for soldiers, fearing indulgence that would make troops arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Anshi had argued: "Soldiers are so destitute that some wear paper under their armor—this is the gravest concern. Yet commanders dare not seek relief for fear of spoiling the ranks and making troops arrogant.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為親士卒如愛子，故可與之俱死；

translations.literal: Your servant thinks that treating soldiers as dearly as one's own children is why one can die with them;
translations.idiomatic: I believe that treating soldiers as one treats one's own children is what makes men willing to die with you;

sentences.zh: 愛而不能令，譬如驕子不可用也。

translations.literal: to love yet be unable to command is like a spoiled child—unusable.
translations.idiomatic: but love without discipline is like a spoiled child—good for nothing.

sentences.zh: 前陛下言郭進事，臣案《進傳》，言進知人疾苦，所至人為立碑紀德；

translations.literal: Earlier Your Majesty spoke of Guo Jin; your servant consulted the Biography of Jin, which says Jin knew people's hardships, and wherever he went people erected steles recording his virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty once mentioned Guo Jin. His biography records that he understood his men's hardships and that people erected steles to his memory wherever he served;

sentences.zh: 士卒小有違令，輒殺之。

translations.literal: for the smallest violation of orders by a soldier, he immediately executed them.
translations.idiomatic: yet he executed soldiers for the smallest breach of orders.

sentences.zh: 惟其能犒賞存恤，然後能殺違令者而人無怨。

translations.literal: Only because he could reward, bestow, and care for them could he then execute violators of orders without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Only because he rewarded and cared for his men could he execute offenders without provoking resentment.

sentences.zh: 今宜稍寬牽拘將帥之法，使得用封樁錢物隨宜振恤，然後可以責將帥得士卒死力也。」

translations.literal: Now the restrictive laws binding commanders should be slightly relaxed, allowing them to use sealed reserve funds to provide relief as appropriate—only then can commanders be required to obtain soldiers' utmost effort."
translations.idiomatic: Relax the rules that bind commanders and let them use sealed reserve funds to relieve hardship as needed—only then can we demand that generals win their men's utmost loyalty."

sentences.zh: 四年，樞密院言：「不教閱廂軍撥並，各帶舊請外，今後招到者，並乞依本指揮新定請受。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Bureau of Military Affairs said: "Undrilled garrison troops merged by transfer each retain their old stipends; for those recruited hereafter, all beg to follow the newly fixed allowances of the original command.
translations.idiomatic: In 1071 the Bureau of Military Affairs reported: "Merged undrilled garrison troops keep their old allowances; newly recruited men should receive the newly fixed rates of their command.

sentences.zh: 河北崇勝、河東雄猛、陝西保寧、京東奉化、京西壯武、淮南寧淮各醬菜錢一百，月糧二石，春衣絹二匹、布半匹、錢一千，冬衣絹二匹、紬半匹、錢一千、綿十二兩。

translations.literal: Hebei Chongsheng, Hedong Xiongmeng, Shaanxi Baoning, Jingdong Fenghua, Jingxi Zhuangwu, and Huainan Ninghuai—each one hundred cash sauce-and-vegetable money, two shi monthly grain, spring clothing two bolts silk, half bolt cloth, one thousand cash; winter clothing two bolts silk, half bolt hemp, one thousand cash, twelve liang cotton.
translations.idiomatic: For Hebei Chongsheng, Hedong Xiongmeng, Shaanxi Baoning, Jingdong Fenghua, Jingxi Zhuangwu, and Huainan Ninghuai: sauce-and-vegetable money of one hundred cash, two shi monthly grain, spring clothing of two bolts silk plus half a bolt of cloth and one thousand cash, winter clothing of two bolts silk plus half a bolt of hemp, one thousand cash, and twelve liang of cotton.

sentences.zh: 兩浙崇節、江東西效勇、荊南北宣節、福建保節、廣東西清化除醬菜錢不支外，餘如六路。

translations.literal: Two-Zhe Chongjie, Jiangdong and Jiangxi Xiaoyong, Jingnan North and South Xuanjie, Fujian Baojie, and Guangdong and Guangxi Qinghua—except that sauce-and-vegetable money is not disbursed—all else as the six circuits.
translations.idiomatic: For Two-Zhe Chongjie, Jiangdong and Jiangxi Xiaoyong, Jingnan North and South Xuanjie, Fujian Baojie, and Guangdong-Guangxi Qinghua, sauce-and-vegetable money was omitted; all other allowances matched the six circuits above.

sentences.zh: 川四路克寧已上各小鐵錢一千，糧二石，春衣絹一匹、小鐵錢十千，冬衣絹一匹、紬一匹、綿八兩、小鐵錢五千。」

translations.literal: The four Sichuan circuits, Kening and above—each one thousand small iron coins, two shi grain, spring clothing one bolt silk and ten thousand small iron coins; winter clothing one bolt silk, one bolt hemp, eight liang cotton, five thousand small iron coins."
translations.idiomatic: In the four Sichuan circuits, Kening and related units received one thousand small iron coins, two shi of grain, spring clothing of one bolt of silk plus ten thousand small iron coins, and winter clothing of one bolt of silk, one bolt of hemp, eight liang of cotton, and five thousand small iron coins."

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 七年，增橋道、清塞、雄勝諸軍奉滿三百。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, stipends for Qiaodao, Qingse, Xionsheng, and related armies were increased to a full three hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: In 1074 stipends for Qiaodao, Qingse, Xionsheng, and related units were raised to a full three hundred cash.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「今後募禁軍等賞給，並減舊兵之半。」

translations.literal: Another edict said: "Hereafter recruitment rewards for Imperial Guard and similar units shall all be reduced to half those of veteran troops."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict cut recruitment bonuses for newly enlisted Imperial Guard troops to half the reward given veteran soldiers.

sentences.zh: 十年，詔：「安南道死戰沒者，所假衣奉咸蠲除之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, an edict said: "For those killed in fierce battle on the Annam route, all borrowed clothing stipends shall be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1077 an edict remitted all borrowed clothing stipends owed by soldiers killed in battle on the Annam expedition.

sentences.zh: 弓箭手、民兵、義勇等有貸於官者，展償限一年。

translations.literal: Archers, militia, and righteous-army troops who had loans from the government received a one-year extension on repayment.
translations.idiomatic: Archers, militia, and righteous-army troops with outstanding government loans received a one-year extension on repayment.

sentences.zh: 又中外禁軍有定額，而三司及諸路歲給諸軍亦有常數。

translations.literal: Furthermore, Imperial Guard units inside and outside the capital had fixed quotas, and the State Fiscal Commission and the various circuits also had fixed annual disbursements for the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Guard units empire-wide had fixed quotas, and the State Fiscal Commission and circuit authorities had fixed annual disbursement schedules for each army.

sentences.zh: 其闕額未補者，會其歲給並封樁，樞密承旨司簿其餘數，輒移用，論如法。」

translations.literal: For unfilled vacancies, the annual disbursement was pooled and sealed; the Bureau of Military Affairs directive office recorded the surplus; unauthorized transfer was punished according to law."
translations.idiomatic: Unfilled quota funds were pooled and sealed; the Bureau of Military Affairs directive office recorded the surplus, and unauthorized diversion was punishable by law."

sentences.zh: 元豐二年，詔：「荊南雄略軍十二營南戍，瘴沒者眾，其議優恤之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanfeng, an edict said: "The twelve camps of the Jingnan Xionglüe Army garrisoning the south—many have perished from miasma; discuss preferential relief for them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1079 an edict ordered: "Twelve camps of the Jingnan Xionglüe Army garrisoning the south have lost many men to miasma—propose preferential relief.

sentences.zh: 軍校子孫降授職。

translations.literal: Officers' descendants were granted appointments at reduced rank.
translations.idiomatic: Officers' descendants received appointments at reduced rank.

sentences.zh: 有疾及不願為兵若無子孫者，加賜緡錢；

translations.literal: Those with illness, unwilling to serve as soldiers, or without descendants received additional strings of cash;
translations.idiomatic: Men who were ill, unwilling to serve, or left without heirs received bonus payments in strings of cash;

sentences.zh: 軍士子孫弟侄收為兵，並給賻，除籍後仍給糧兩月；

translations.literal: When soldiers' sons, grandsons, younger brothers, or nephews were enrolled as troops, burial grants were also given; after removal from the rolls, grain was still issued for two months;
translations.idiomatic: When a soldier's sons, grandsons, younger brothers, or nephews were taken into service, burial allowances were paid; after discharge from the rolls, rations continued for two months;

sentences.zh: 即父母年七十已上無子孫者，給衣廩之半，終其身。」

translations.literal: For parents seventy and above without descendants, half of clothing and ration allowances was granted for life."
translations.idiomatic: Parents seventy or older who had lost all descendants received half their son's clothing and ration allowance for life."

sentences.zh: 哲宗即位，悉依舊制。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong acceded, everything followed the former regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong came to the throne, all provisions reverted to the established rules.

sentences.zh: 徽宗崇寧四年，詔：「諸軍料錢不多，比聞支當十錢，恐難分用，自今可止給小平錢。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongning under Emperor Huizong, an edict said: "The ration money of the various armies is limited; I have lately heard that ten-cash pieces are issued in payment, which are hard to divide for use—from now on only standard small flat coins shall be issued."
translations.idiomatic: In 1105 Emperor Huizong ordered: "Army ration allowances are modest, yet I hear ten-cash pieces are being paid out and are hard to spend—hereafter only standard small flat coins are to be issued."

sentences.zh: 初，蔡京謀逐王恩，計不行，欲陰結環衛及諸士卒，乃奏皇城輔兵月給食錢五百者，日給一百五十。

translations.literal: At first, Cai Jing plotted to drive out Wang En; when the scheme failed, wishing to win over secretly the palace guards and various soldiers, he memorialized that auxiliary troops of the Imperial Palace City who received five hundred cash monthly food money should receive one hundred fifty per day.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Cai Jing had tried to oust Wang En. When that failed, he sought to win over palace guards and common soldiers by proposing that Imperial Palace City auxiliaries on 500-cash monthly food allowances receive 150 cash per day.

sentences.zh: 自是，每月頓增四貫五百。

translations.literal: From this, each month suddenly increased by four strings five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: This raised each man's monthly pay by four and a half strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 欲因以市私恩也。

translations.literal: He intended by this to purchase private favor.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to buy personal loyalty this way.

sentences.zh: 五年，樞密院言：「自熙寧以來，封樁隸樞密院，比因創招廣勇、崇捷、崇武十萬人，權撥封樁入尚書省。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the Bureau of Military Affairs said: "Since Xining, sealed reserves have belonged to the Bureau of Military Affairs; recently because of recruiting one hundred thousand Guangyong, Chongjie, and Chongwu troops, sealed reserves were temporarily transferred to the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1106 the Bureau of Military Affairs reported: "Since the Xining reforms sealed reserve funds have belonged to the Bureau, but the recent recruitment of 100,000 Guangyong, Chongjie, and Chongwu troops temporarily diverted those funds to the central fiscal authorities.

sentences.zh: 緣禁軍見闕數多，若專責戶部及轉運司應副，恐致誤事。」

translations.literal: Because Imperial Guard vacancies at present are numerous, if the Ministry of Revenue and transport commissioners alone are charged with supply, I fear matters may go wrong."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Guard vacancies are numerous; relying solely on the Ministry of Revenue and circuit transport offices to meet them risks failure."

sentences.zh: 詔：「尚書省候極足十萬人外，理合撥還。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Apart from what the Imperial Secretariat needs to fill the one hundred thousand recruits, the rest should properly be returned.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered: "Once the central authorities had filled the 100,000 recruits, the surplus sealed funds must be returned.

sentences.zh: 自今應禁軍闕額封樁錢，仍隸樞密院。」

translations.literal: From now on sealed reserve funds for Imperial Guard vacancy quotas still belong to the Bureau of Military Affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth sealed reserve funds for unfilled Imperial Guard quotas shall remain under the Bureau of Military Affairs."

sentences.zh: 宣和七年，詔：「國家養兵，衣食豐足。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xuanhe, an edict said: "The state maintains soldiers with abundant clothing and food.
translations.idiomatic: In 1125 an edict declared: "The state supports its troops with generous clothing and food.

sentences.zh: 近歲以來，官不守法，侵奪者多；

translations.literal: In recent years officials have not obeyed the law; encroachments and seizures have been many;
translations.idiomatic: In recent years officials have ignored the law, and diversions have multiplied;

sentences.zh: 若軍司乞取及因事率斂，刻剝分數，反致不足。

translations.literal: when army offices begged for funds and used pretexts to levy, carving and stripping fractional shares, the result was actually insufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: when army offices solicited bribes and levied arbitrary fees, shaving fractional shares until the men lacked enough.

sentences.zh: 又官吏冗占猥多，修造役使，違法差借。

translations.literal: Furthermore redundant occupation by officials was excessive; construction and forced service involved unlawful requisition and borrowing.
translations.idiomatic: Officers filled posts redundantly, and construction and corvée duty involved illegal impressment.

sentences.zh: 雜役之兵，食浮於禁旅，假借之卒，役重於廂軍。

translations.literal: Miscellaneous-service soldiers ate better than Imperial Guard ranks; borrowed soldiers were worked harder than garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous-service troops ate better than Imperial Guard units, while borrowed soldiers were worked harder than garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 近因整緝軍政，深駭聽聞。

translations.literal: Recently in rectifying military administration, this deeply shocked the court.
translations.idiomatic: A recent overhaul of military administration exposed abuses that shocked the court.

sentences.zh: 自今違戾如前者，重寘之法。」

translations.literal: From now on violators as before shall be punished by heavy penalties."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth offenders will face severe punishment."

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，詔：「諸路州軍二稅課利，先行樁辦軍兵合支每月糧料、春衣、冬賜數足，方許別行支散官吏請給等。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, an edict said: "In every circuit's prefectures and garrisons, two-tax revenues and commercial levies must first be earmarked in full for soldiers' monthly grain and ration money, spring clothing, and winter grants—only then may officials' stipends and the like be disbursed separately.
translations.idiomatic: In 1126 an edict ordered that across every circuit, two-tax revenues and commercial levies must first cover soldiers' monthly grain and ration allowances, spring clothing, and winter grants in full before any official stipends could be paid.

sentences.zh: 禁軍月糧，並免坐倉。

translations.literal: Imperial Guard monthly grain rations were all exempt from warehouse conversion.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Guard monthly grain was paid directly, without warehouse conversion.

sentences.zh: 自國初以來，內則三司，外則漕台，率以軍儲為急務，故錢糧支賜，歲有定數。

translations.literal: Since the founding of the dynasty, within the State Fiscal Commission and without the transport offices, military stores have generally been the urgent task; thus cash-and-grain disbursements and grants have fixed annual amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Since the dynasty's founding the State Fiscal Commission within and transport commissioners without have treated military stores as their foremost duty, and cash-and-grain disbursements were fixed year by year.

sentences.zh: 至於征戍調發之特支，將士功勞之犒賞，與夫諸軍闕額而收其奉廩以為上供之封樁者，雖無定數，而未嘗無權衡於其間也。

translations.literal: As for special disbursements for campaign and garrison deployment, rewards for officers' and soldiers' merit, and the collection of stipend rations from army vacancy quotas as sealed tribute to the capital—though without fixed numbers, balance was never wholly absent.
translations.idiomatic: Special payments for campaigns and deployments, merit rewards, and sealed reserves drawn from unfilled quota stipends all lacked fixed sums, yet were never wholly unregulated.

sentences.zh: 封樁累朝皆有之，而熙寧為盛。

translations.literal: Sealed reserves existed in every reign, and Xining was the peak.
translations.idiomatic: Sealed reserve funds existed under every reign, but peaked in the Xining era.

sentences.zh: 其後雖有「今後再不封樁」之詔，然軍司告乏，則暫從其請，稍或優足，則封樁如舊。

translations.literal: Although afterward there was an edict saying "henceforth no more sealed reserves," when army offices reported shortage their pleas were temporarily granted; once slightly ample, sealed reserves resumed as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later edicts declared "no more sealed reserves," yet when army offices cried shortage the court relented—and once funds were ample, sealing resumed.

sentences.zh: 蓋宰執得人，則闕額用於朝遷；

translations.literal: For when the chief ministers were capable men, vacancy quotas were used for court transfer;
translations.idiomatic: When capable chief ministers held power, vacancy funds went to court transfers;

sentences.zh: 樞筦勢重，則闕額歸之密院。

translations.literal: when the Bureau of Military Affairs was powerful, vacancy quotas returned to the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: when the Bureau of Military Affairs held sway, vacancy funds reverted to the Bureau.

sentences.zh: 此政和軍政所以益不逮於崇寧、大觀之間者，由兩府之勢互有輕重，而不能恪守祖宗之法也。

translations.literal: This is why Zhenghe military administration increasingly fell short of the Chongning and Daguan periods: because the power of the two councils alternately waxed and waned, and they could not steadfastly uphold ancestral law.
translations.idiomatic: This is why Zhenghe military administration declined from the Chongning and Daguan standards—the two councils' shifting balance of power prevented faithful adherence to ancestral regulations.

sentences.zh: 中興以後，多遵舊制。

translations.literal: After the Restoration, old regulations were largely followed.
translations.idiomatic: After the Southern Song restoration, most provisions followed earlier rules.

sentences.zh: 紹興四年，御前軍器所言：「萬全雜役額五百，戶部廩給有常法。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaoxing, the Imperial Armory directorate said: "The Wanquan miscellaneous service quota is five hundred; the Ministry of Revenue has fixed regulations for ration allowances.
translations.idiomatic: In 1134 the Imperial Armory directorate reported: "The Wanquan miscellaneous-service quota is 500 men, with fixed Ministry of Revenue ration scales.

sentences.zh: 比申明裁減，盡皆遁逃。

translations.literal: Recently when the clarified reductions were announced, all fled.
translations.idiomatic: After announced cuts, every man deserted.

sentences.zh: 若依部所定月米五斗五升，日不及二升；

translations.literal: If the Ministry's fixed monthly rice of five dou five sheng is followed, daily it falls short of two sheng;
translations.idiomatic: At the Ministry rate of five dou five sheng monthly rice, a man received less than two sheng per day;

sentences.zh: 麥四斗八升，鬥折錢二百，日餐錢百，實不足贍。」

translations.literal: wheat four dou eight sheng, converted at two hundred cash per dou, daily meal money one hundred—it truly did not suffice to support them."
translations.idiomatic: plus four dou eight sheng of wheat converted at two hundred cash per dou and one hundred cash daily meal money—hardly enough to live on.

sentences.zh: 詔戶部裁定，月米一石七斗，增作一石九斗。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Ministry of Revenue to decide: monthly rice one shi seven dou, increased to one shi nine dou.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue was ordered to raise monthly rice from one shi seven dou to one shi nine dou.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔：「效用入資舊法，內公據、甲頭名稱未正，其改公據為守闕進勇副尉，日餐錢二百五十、米二升；

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict said: "Under the old law for utility-troop paid entry, the titles of service certificates and squad heads were not rectified; change service certificates to Candidate Advance Brave Vice Commandant, daily meal money two hundred fifty and rice two sheng;
translations.idiomatic: In 1135 an edict reformed utility-troop paid-entry titles: service certificates became Candidate Advance Brave Vice Commandant, with 250 cash and two sheng of rice daily;

sentences.zh: 甲頭為進勇副尉，日餐錢二百、米二升。

translations.literal: squad heads to Advance Brave Vice Commandant, daily meal money two hundred and rice two sheng.
translations.idiomatic: squad leaders became Advance Brave Vice Commandant, with 200 cash and two sheng of rice daily.

sentences.zh: 非帶甲入隊人自依舊法。」

translations.literal: Those not entering ranks in armor followed the old law."
translations.idiomatic: Men not entering in armor remained under the old rules.

sentences.zh: 宣撫使韓世忠言：「本軍調發，老幼隨行，緣效用內有不調月糧，不增給日請，軍兵米二升半、錢百，效用米二升、錢二百，乞日增給贍米一升半，庶幾戰士無家累後顧憂，齊心用命。」

translations.literal: Pacification commissioner Han Shizhong said: "When this army deploys, old and young follow along; because some utility troops receive no monthly grain adjustment and no increase in daily allowance—regular soldiers get two and a half sheng rice and one hundred cash, utility troops two sheng and two hundred cash—I beg a daily supplemental rice allowance of one and a half sheng, so that fighting men may be free of worries over family burdens and serve with one heart."
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioner Han Shizhong argued: "When my army deploys, families follow. Some utility troops receive no monthly grain and no daily increase—regular soldiers get two and a half sheng of rice and one hundred cash daily, utility troops two sheng and two hundred cash. I ask one and a half sheng supplemental rice daily so warriors need not fear for their families and will fight as one.

sentences.zh: 詔分屯日即陳請。

translations.literal: An edict said: when stationed at separate posts they may submit the request immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were to submit requests as soon as they took up separate garrisons.

sentences.zh: 十三年，詔：「殿司諸統領將官別無供給職田，日贍不足，差兵營運，浸壞軍政。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, an edict said: "Palace Bureau unit commanders and officers have no supply lands for support; daily provisions are insufficient, and assigning soldiers to carry and trade gradually ruins military administration.
translations.idiomatic: In 1143 an edict noted that Palace Bureau unit leaders lacked support lands, daily rations fell short, and impressing soldiers for transport and trade was undermining military discipline.

sentences.zh: 可與月支供給：統製、副統製月一百五十千，統領官百千，正將、同正將五十千，副將四十千，準備將三十千，皆按月給。

translations.literal: Monthly supply grants may be given: unit commander and deputy commander one hundred fifty thousand per month, unit leader one hundred thousand, chief and associate chief fifty thousand, vice chief forty thousand, reserve chief thirty thousand—all paid monthly.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly allowances were granted: unit commanders and deputies 150,000 cash, unit leaders 100,000, chief and associate chiefs 50,000, vice chiefs 40,000, reserve chiefs 30,000—all paid monthly.

sentences.zh: 既足其家，可責後效。

translations.literal: Once their households are provided for, later performance can be demanded.
translations.idiomatic: Once their families were provided for, the court could demand results.

sentences.zh: 若仍前差兵負販，從私役禁軍法，所販物計贓坐之，必罰無赦。

translations.literal: If they still assign soldiers to carry goods for sale as before, follow the Imperial Guard private-service law; goods sold count for loot in sentencing, punishment without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers impressed for peddling would be punished under Imperial Guard private-service law, with goods counted as stolen property—no mercy.

sentences.zh: 州縣知而不舉，同罪。」

translations.literal: Prefecture and county officials who knew and did not report, same penalty."
translations.idiomatic: Local officials who knew and failed to report faced the same penalty.

sentences.zh: 主管步軍司趙密言：「比定諸軍五等請給，招填闕額，要以屏革奸弊。

translations.literal: Director of the Infantry Bureau Zhao Mi said: "Recent fixed five-grade allowances for the various armies, recruiting to fill vacancies, intended to eliminate corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Infantry Bureau director Zhao Mi reported: "The recent five-grade allowance system was meant to fill vacancies and root out corruption.

sentences.zh: 第數內招收白身效用，填馬步軍使臣闕。

translations.literal: Among the grades white-body utility troops were recruited to fill cavalry and infantry officer vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: Within those grades, raw recruits were taken as utility troops to fill cavalry and infantry officer vacancies.

sentences.zh: 其五等請給例內，馬軍效用依五人衙官例，步軍效用依三人衙官例。

translations.literal: Within the five-grade allowance precedent, cavalry utility troops followed the five-man gate-officer precedent; infantry utility troops followed the three-man gate-officer precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Under the five-grade scales, cavalry utility troops matched the five-man gate-officer rate and infantry utility troops the three-man gate-officer rate.

sentences.zh: 緣舊效用曾經帶甲出入，日止餐錢二百、米二升；

translations.literal: Because old utility troops had borne armor in and out, daily only meal money two hundred and rice two sheng;
translations.idiomatic: Veteran utility troops who had served in armor received only two hundred cash and two sheng of rice daily;

sentences.zh: 有少壯善射者，既見初收效用廩給稍優，因逃他軍以希厚請。

translations.literal: some young and strong skilled archers, seeing newly recruited utility troops' rations slightly better, fled to other armies hoping for richer allowances.
translations.idiomatic: Able young archers deserted to other units hoping for the richer allowances granted newly recruited utility troops.

sentences.zh: 今擬五等招收白身效用與舊效用，不以馬步軍論，概增其給，人日支錢二百、米二升，填使臣闕。」

translations.literal: Now it is proposed that fifth-grade recruited white-body utility troops and old utility troops, regardless of cavalry or infantry, all have allowances uniformly increased: per man daily two hundred cash and two sheng rice, filling officer vacancies."
translations.idiomatic: We propose uniform increases for new and veteran utility troops regardless of branch: two hundred cash and two sheng of rice daily, to fill officer vacancies."

sentences.zh: 隆興二年，殿前司言：「諸軍法，兵級年六十，將校年六十五，減充剩員給請，內有戰功亦止半給。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longxing, the Palace Bureau said: "Under army law, soldiers at sixty and officers at sixty-five are reduced to surplus rolls for pay; even those with battle merit receive only half.
translations.idiomatic: In 1164 the Palace Bureau reported: "Under army law, soldiers at sixty and officers at sixty-five are placed on surplus rolls; even men with battle merit receive only half pay.

sentences.zh: 比來年及不與減落，乞每營置籍，鄉貫、年甲、招刺日月悉書之，一留本營，一留戶部，一留總領，以備開落。」

translations.literal: Recently when age was reached they were not reduced; I beg that each camp keep registers recording native place, age, and recruitment date—one kept at the camp, one at the Ministry of Revenue, one at the overall supervisor—to prepare for opening and closing rolls."
translations.idiomatic: Men have not been retired on schedule. We ask each camp to keep registers noting birthplace, age, and enlistment date—copies at camp, Ministry of Revenue, and chief supervisor—to manage roll reductions."

sentences.zh: 乾道八年，樞密院言：「二月為始，諸軍七人例以上，二分錢、三分銀、五分會子；

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Qiandao, the Bureau of Military Affairs said: "Beginning in the second month, for armies at the seven-man stipend level and above, two parts cash, three parts silver, five parts paper notes;
translations.idiomatic: In 1172 the Bureau ordered that from the second month, units on seven-man stipends or higher would receive two parts cash, three parts silver, and five parts paper notes;

sentences.zh: 五人例，三分錢、四分銀、三分會子。

translations.literal: for the five-man level, three parts cash, four parts silver, three parts paper notes.
translations.idiomatic: five-man stipend units would receive three parts cash, four parts silver, and three parts paper notes.

sentences.zh: 軍兵折麥餐錢，全支錢。

translations.literal: For soldiers' wheat-converted meal money, full payment in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers' wheat-conversion meal allowances were paid entirely in cash.

sentences.zh: 使臣折麥、料錢，統製、軍佐供給分數仍舊。」

translations.literal: Officers' wheat-conversion and ration money, unit commanders' and staff adjutants' supply shares remain as before."
translations.idiomatic: Officers' wheat conversion and ration allowances, and unit commanders' and adjutants' shares, remained unchanged."

sentences.zh: 淳熙三年，樞密院言：「兵部定請受格：效用一資守闕毅士，二資毅士，三資守闕效士，月各錢三千，折麥錢七百二十，米一石五升，春冬衣絹各二匹；

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunxi, the Bureau of Military Affairs said: "The Ministry of War fixed allowance scales: utility troops at one rank Candidate Resolute Soldier, two ranks Resolute Soldier, three ranks Candidate Effective Soldier—each month three thousand cash, wheat-conversion money seven hundred twenty, rice one shi five sheng, spring and winter two bolts silk each;
translations.idiomatic: In 1176 the Bureau reported the Ministry of War's allowance scales: utility troops at one rank Candidate Resolute Soldier, two ranks Resolute Soldier, and three ranks Candidate Effective Soldier each received 3,000 cash monthly, 720 wheat-conversion cash, one shi five sheng of rice, and two bolts of silk for spring and winter clothing;

sentences.zh: 四資效士，錢三千，折麥錢九百七十二，米一石一斗三升有奇，衣絹各二匹；

translations.literal: four ranks Effective Soldier: three thousand cash, wheat-conversion nine hundred seventy-two, rice one shi one dou three sheng odd, two bolts silk each;
translations.idiomatic: fourth rank Effective Soldier: 3,000 cash, 972 wheat-conversion cash, one shi one dou and a fraction of rice, two bolts of silk each;

sentences.zh: 五資守闕聽候使喚，錢四千五百，折麥錢一千八十，米一石二斗，絹三匹有半；

translations.literal: five ranks Candidate Awaiting Summons: four thousand five hundred cash, wheat-conversion one thousand eighty, rice one shi two dou, three and a half bolts silk;
translations.idiomatic: fifth rank Candidate Awaiting Summons: 4,500 cash, 1,080 wheat-conversion cash, one shi two dou of rice, three and a half bolts of silk;

sentences.zh: 六資聽候使喚，錢四千五百，折麥錢一千二百六十，米一石四斗七升，絹五匹；

translations.literal: six ranks Awaiting Summons: four thousand five hundred cash, wheat-conversion one thousand two hundred sixty, rice one shi four dou seven sheng, five bolts silk;
translations.idiomatic: sixth rank Awaiting Summons: 4,500 cash, 1,260 wheat-conversion cash, one shi four dou seven sheng of rice, five bolts of silk;

sentences.zh: 七資守闕聽候差使，八資聽候差使，錢四千五百，折麥錢一千四百四十，米一石六斗八升，絹各五匹；

translations.literal: seven ranks Candidate Awaiting Assignment, eight ranks Awaiting Assignment: four thousand five hundred cash, wheat-conversion one thousand four hundred forty, rice one shi six dou eight sheng, five bolts silk each;
translations.idiomatic: seventh rank Candidate Awaiting Assignment and eighth rank Awaiting Assignment: 4,500 cash, 1,440 wheat-conversion cash, one shi six dou eight sheng of rice, five bolts of silk each;

sentences.zh: 九資守闕準備使喚，十資準備差使，錢五千，折麥錢一千四百四十，米六石八升，絹各五匹。」

translations.literal: nine ranks Candidate Ready Summons, ten ranks Ready Assignment: five thousand cash, wheat-conversion one thousand four hundred forty, rice six shi eight sheng, five bolts silk each."
translations.idiomatic: ninth rank Candidate Ready Summons and tenth rank Ready Assignment: 5,000 cash, 1,440 wheat-conversion cash, six shi eight sheng of rice, five bolts of silk each."

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年，知常德府王銖言：「沿邊城砦之官，以備疆埸不虞，廩祿既薄，給不以時，孤寒小吏，何以養廉？

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi, prefect of Changde Wang Zhu said: "Border fort officials garrisoned against frontier emergencies have thin stipends paid irregularly—how can poor minor clerks preserve integrity?
translations.idiomatic: In 1190 Changde prefect Wang Zhu memorialized: "Border fort officials guarding against frontier emergencies receive thin stipends paid late—how can impoverished clerks remain honest?

sentences.zh: 致使熟視奸猾泄漏禁物，公私庇蓋，恬不加問，從而徇私受賕者有矣。

translations.literal: This leads them to watch complacently as scoundrels smuggle contraband, shielding them publicly and privately without inquiry, and some even take bribes for private favor.
translations.idiomatic: They look on as smugglers move contraband, shielding them in public and private without inquiry—and some take bribes.

sentences.zh: 弓手、士軍、戍卒傭直糧食，累月不支，迫於饑寒，侵漁蠻獠，小則致訟爭，大則啟邊釁。

translations.literal: Bowmen, local garrison troops, and garrison soldiers' wages and grain unpaid for months—in hunger and cold they encroach on tribal peoples; small matters cause lawsuits, large ones provoke border conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Bowmen, local troops, and garrison soldiers went unpaid for months; driven by hunger and cold they preyed on tribal peoples—sparking lawsuits at best and border clashes at worst.

sentences.zh: 乞嚴敕州、軍按月廩給，如其未支，守倅即不得先請己奉。

translations.literal: I beg strict orders that prefectures and garrisons pay rations monthly; if unpaid, prefects and deputies must not draw their own salaries first.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that prefectures and garrisons pay rations monthly on pain of penalty, and that prefects and deputies draw no salary until their men are paid.

sentences.zh: 庶俾城砦官兵有以存濟，緩急之際，得其宣力。

translations.literal: Then fort officials and soldiers may survive, and in emergencies serve effectively.
translations.idiomatic: Then fort garrisons could subsist and serve effectively in emergencies.

sentences.zh: 安邊弭盜，莫此為急。」

translations.literal: Securing the border and suppressing banditry—nothing is more urgent."
translations.idiomatic: Securing the frontier and suppressing banditry—nothing was more urgent."

sentences.zh: 厥後弊日以滋，迨至咸淳，軍將往往虛立員以冒稍食。

translations.literal: Thereafter abuses daily multiplied; by Xianchun, army officers often fictitiously created posts to claim stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Abuses multiplied thereafter; by the Xianchun era army officers routinely created phantom posts to collect stipends.

sentences.zh: 以建康言之，有神策二軍，有遊擊五軍，有親兵二軍，有制效二軍，有靖安、唐灣水軍，有遊擊采石水軍，有精銳破敵軍，有效用、防江軍，原其初起，惟騎、戎兩司額耳。

translations.literal: Taking Jiankang as example: there were two Shence armies, five Youji armies, two personal-guard armies, two Zhixiao armies, Jing'an and Tangwan naval forces, Youji Caishi naval forces, the Jingrui Pode army, utility and river-defense armies—tracing their origin, there were only the quotas of the two cavalry and infantry bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiankang alone there were two Shence armies, five Youji armies, two personal-guard armies, two Zhixiao armies, Jing'an and Tangwan naval units, Youji Caishi naval forces, the Jingrui Pode army, and utility and river-defense armies—yet originally there had been only the quotas of the cavalry and infantry bureaus.

sentences.zh: 後仍各創軍分，額多而員少。

translations.literal: Later each still created separate army divisions; quotas were many but personnel few.
translations.idiomatic: Later each command spawned new army divisions—quotas swelled while actual head counts shrank.

sentences.zh: 一統製月請，以會子計之，則成一萬五百千，推之他軍，概可見矣。

translations.literal: One unit commander's monthly allowance, reckoned in paper notes, came to ten thousand five hundred strings; extrapolate to other armies and the pattern is clear.
translations.idiomatic: One unit commander's monthly allowance, reckoned in paper notes, reached 10,500 strings of cash—the same pattern held across every army.

sentences.zh: 九年，四川製司有言：「戍兵生券，人月給會子六千，蜀郡物賈翔貴，請增人月給九千。」

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the Sichuan commandery reported: "Garrison soldiers' living certificates pay six thousand paper notes monthly; Sichuan prices soar—I beg increase to nine thousand per man monthly."
translations.idiomatic: In 1273 the Sichuan command reported: "Garrison soldiers' living certificates paid 6,000 paper notes monthly, but Sichuan prices had soared—it requested 9,000 per man.

sentences.zh: 當是時財賦之出有限，廩稍之給無涯，浚民膏血，盡充邊費，金帛悉歸於二三大將之私帑，國用益竭，而宋亡矣。

translations.literal: By then fiscal outlay was finite but ration grants boundless; draining the people's blood to fill border costs, gold and silk all went to a few great generals' private treasuries; state coffers depleted—and Song perished.
translations.idiomatic: By then revenue was finite but military rations limitless. The state drained the people's wealth to fund the frontier while gold and silk flowed into a few great generals' private coffers. The treasury emptied—and Song fell.

sentences.zh: 臣僚嘗言：「古者兵與農一，官無供億之煩，國有備禦之責。

translations.literal: Officials once said: "Anciently soldiers and farmers were one; officials had no supply burden, the state had defense duty.
translations.idiomatic: Officials once argued: "In antiquity soldier and farmer were one; officials bore no supply burden and the state held defense as its duty.

sentences.zh: 後世兵與農二，竭國力以養兵，奉之若驕子，用之若傭人。

translations.literal: Later soldiers and farmers were two; exhausting national strength to maintain troops, cherishing them like spoiled sons yet using them like hired laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Later soldier and farmer parted; the state exhausted its strength to feed an army it pampered like spoiled children yet employed like hired labor.

sentences.zh: 今守邊急務，非兵農合一不可。

translations.literal: Today the urgent task of guarding the frontier cannot be done without reuniting soldiers and farmers.
translations.idiomatic: Guarding the frontier today cannot succeed without reuniting soldier and farmer.

sentences.zh: 其說者有二：曰屯田，曰民兵。

translations.literal: There are two proposals: frontier farming colonies and militia.
translations.idiomatic: Two proposals were offered: frontier farming colonies and militia.

sentences.zh: 川蜀屯田為先，民兵次之；

translations.literal: In Sichuan-Shu, frontier farming colonies first, militia second;
translations.idiomatic: In Sichuan, frontier colonies should come first and militia second;

sentences.zh: 淮、襄民兵為先，屯田次之。

translations.literal: On the Huai and Xiang frontiers, militia first, frontier farming colonies second.
translations.idiomatic: On the Huai and Xiang frontiers, militia should come first and frontier colonies second.

sentences.zh: 此足食足兵之良策也。」

translations.literal: These are excellent policies for ample food and ample troops."
translations.idiomatic: These were sound policies for securing both food and troops.

sentences.zh: 其言厄於權奸，竟不行。

translations.literal: Their proposals were blocked by powerful villains and were never implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Their proposals were blocked by powerful faction leaders and were never carried out.
